sections.title: 2. Who the exam is for
sections.html:
As a candidate for this Microsoft Certification, you’re a professional who builds AI-powered solutions in Microsoft Power Platform by using Microsoft Copilot, natural language prompts, and low-code tools. You create apps, data models, and flows that connect to agents, AI models and prompts, and visualizations to enrich these experiences.

In this role, your responsibilities include:

  • Developing Dataverse data models, model-driven apps, and canvas apps.
  • Integrating agents and Copilot features into canvas apps, model-driven apps, and Power Pages sites.
  • Creating cloud flows and business logic.

You collaborate with:

  • Environment and security administrators for policies, roles, identity, and authentication.
  • Governance teams on responsible AI principles, application lifecycle management (ALM), solutions, pipelines, and monitoring.
  • Agent developers, solution architects, and other app builders for business solution building.
  • Business stakeholders to gather requirements, iterate business solutions, and promote user adoption.

For this exam, you should have experience with:

  • Using natural language to create solution assets.
  • Dataverse modeling.
  • Power Automate cloud flows.
  • AI capabilities in Microsoft Power Platform.
  • Power Apps development.
  • Power Pages sites.

Prerequisites for the exam include:

  • Familiarity with using Copilot in Power Apps, Copilot in Power Automate, Copilot in Power Pages, and Copilot in Dataverse.
  • Awareness of creating agents with Microsoft Copilot Studio.
  • Foundational knowledge of AI models and prompts in AI Hub.
  • Ability to map business processes to flows, agents, or app capabilities.
  • Ability to work with Dataverse as a core data platform.
  • Familiarity with low-code automation, including Power Fx.
  • Awareness of environment governance, roles, policies, and solution lifecycle steps.

Source: Official study guide (audience profile), updated 2026-10-16.

sections.title: 4. How to read the skills measured
sections.html:
• The bullets illustrate how a skill is assessed; related topics may appear (Microsoft's own note in the study guide). Treat each bullet as a heading for everything around it.
  • Most questions cover generally available (GA) features, but Preview features can appear when they are commonly used. Where the documentation labels something preview, retired or renamed, this guide says so.
  • Expect scenario questions (pick the right setting, path, role or sequence for a requirement) and decision questions (X versus Y). Exact names, menu paths and limits matter.
  • Case studies present a business scenario followed by several questions. Read the requirements and constraints once, then answer every question against them. Microsoft's break rules differ inside case-study and problem/solution sets.

sections.title: What is new in AB-410
sections.html:
Almost everything new is about AI features, agents and design-level decisions: the PL-200 outline has no bullet on Copilot, prompts, AI models or agents. Bullets below are quoted from the AB-410 outline; the numbers are the AB-410 skill groups.

  • New AI-enabled design (1.1): “Analyze requirements to identify components and options for implementation”, “Evaluate built-in agents to include in the business solution” and “Recommend extensibility options”.
  • New Dataverse AI features (1.2): “Configure prompt columns” and “Configure row summaries”; the table bullet now names the data workspace (“Create and edit tables in the data workspace”).
  • New Model-driven apps (2.1): “Create generative pages by using natural language”, “Compose a model-driven app”, “Configure access to model-driven apps” and “Configure access to forms and views for model-driven apps”.
  • New Canvas apps, from “describe” to “create” (2.2): “Create a canvas app using data”, “Design apps for accessibility, performance, responsiveness, and usability”, “Create reuseable components, including named formulas, user-defined functions, and component libraries”, “Test canvas apps, including using Monitor” and “Create a Copilot Studio agent from a canvas app”.
  • New Cloud flow judgement (3.1): “Recommend cloud flow triggers”, “Evaluate and recommend connectors” and “Manage approvals by using cloud flows”.
  • New Prompts and models in AI Hub (3.2), the whole group: “Build prompts from templates or from blank”, “Consume a prompt in apps”, “Consume a prompt in cloud flows”, “Add knowledge to a prompt”, “Customize prompt settings, including models”, “Add inputs to a prompt”, “Consume an AI model in apps” and “Consume an AI model in cloud flows”.
  • New Business logic judgement (3.3): “Evaluate use cases for business logic”.
New prerequisite knowledgeThe AB-410 audience profile lists familiarity with Copilot in Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages and Dataverse, awareness of creating agents with Microsoft Copilot Studio, and foundational knowledge of AI models and prompts in AI Hub. The PL-200 audience profile mentions none of these.

Sources: AB-410 study guide · PL-200 study guide

sections.title: What it means if you studied PL-200
sections.html:
Reuse what you know

  • Carried over Dataverse tables, columns, relationships and table properties; model-driven forms and views; business rules; business process flows; cloud flow control, errors and troubleshooting; Power Fx variables, collections and error handling (now at “create” depth for canvas apps).

Add

  • New The whole AI Hub group (3.2): build prompts from templates or from blank, add inputs and knowledge, change model settings, and consume prompts and AI models in apps and cloud flows.
  • New Prompt columns, row summaries, generative pages, Plans, built-in agents, Live monitor, a Copilot Studio agent from a canvas app, accessible and fast canvas design, reusable formulas and components, approvals, and recommending triggers and connectors.
  • Do not rely on the official course alone for several of these: its canvas modules do not cover Live monitor or building a Copilot Studio agent, and its one AI Hub module builds a prompt from blank without prompt templates, model settings or AI model use. The AI Hub prompt pages now sit in the Copilot Studio documentation.

Lighten

  • Removed Power Pages building, classic workflows, Dataverse search, auditing, duplicate detection and bulk deletion, business units and hierarchy security, solution import and export, and email, SharePoint and Word-template integration are no longer in the outline.

If you hold PL-200 or had it booked

  • Your PL-200 is not revoked: Microsoft says retirement does “not revoke or invalidate” earned certifications and that the credential “remains valid until it expires”; Learn keeps it in the Active section of your transcript until then. It cannot be renewed, because the renewal assessment retired with the exam on 31 Aug 2026.
  • To hold Intelligent Applications Builder Associate you have to pass AB-410; Microsoft describes no direct transition.
  • An exam booked for PL-200 had to be taken by 31 Aug 2026: registration ended the day the exam retired, and a failed attempt cannot be retaken after retirement.
  • AB-410 is offered in 13 languages; PL-200 was offered in seven (English, Chinese (Simplified), French, German, Japanese, Portuguese (Brazil), Spanish).

sections.title: 1.1 Design Microsoft Power Platform solutions by using AI-enabled tools
sections.html:
Skills measured: analyze requirements to identify components and options for implementation • evaluate built-in agents to include in the business solution • recommend extensibility options • recommend environment types • apply a Microsoft Power Platform solution and ALM strategy. Practise by creating a plan, saving it into a solution, and promoting that solution through development, test and production environments with a pipeline.

Analyze requirements to identify components and options for implementation

Start from the business problem, not from a familiar tool. The components are Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Pages, Copilot Studio, AI Builder and Power BI, built around Dataverse (security roles, business rules, relationships, auditing). Most solutions combine several. Ask who uses it, what data (transactional, unstructured documents, analytical), is it human-driven or automated, and is natural language involved.

RequirementPrimary componentTypical additions
Internal app for employeesPower Apps (canvas or model-driven)Dataverse, Power Automate
External customer portalPower PagesDataverse, Copilot Studio web agent
Process automationPower AutomateDataverse, AI Builder
Conversational or autonomous agentCopilot StudioDataverse, Power Automate (agent actions)
Document intelligence (invoices, receipts, forms)AI BuilderPower Automate, Dataverse
Reporting and visualizationPower BIDataverse
  • Learn's Contoso examples: emailed invoices (PDFs and scans) → AI Builder + Power Automate + model-driven app; staff juggling four systems → canvas app plus embedded Copilot Studio agent; clients checking status and uploading documents → Power Pages + Dataverse + web agent; approvals lost in email → Power Automate approval flow with Teams adaptive cards.
  • Canvas or model-driven? Canvas: pixel-level control with Power Fx, Dataverse plus many sources through connectors, task-focused and mobile-friendly. Model-driven: generated from the Dataverse model (forms, views, charts, dashboards), Dataverse only, consistent and responsive, simple to migrate, suited to data-rich work such as case management.
  • AI-first patterns: human-assisted (AI prepares, a person decides), agent-assisted (an agent handles routine steps and escalates), fully autonomous (humans see only exceptions). Use desktop flows for apps without APIs and approval actions for human-in-the-loop steps.
  • Well-Architected PE:03: balance platform features and custom builds, aim custom parts at specific gaps, and weigh team skills.

Plans in Power Apps (the AI-enabled design tool)

Describe the business problem in natural language, attach images (process diagrams, data models, legacy-app screenshots) and Copilot generates a plan. GA, on by default; only Microsoft Support can turn it off. Admin settings still call it plan designer.

TopicWhat to know
Start and limitsmake.powerapps.com > Home > Start with a plan > Create a plan, or Plans in the left navigation. Needs a Dataverse database and an eligible locale; maximum input 4,000 tokens. System Administrator and System Customizer see the entry point; an Environment Maker is redirected to their own developer environment when saving tables.
Plan agents, in orderRequirement Agent (user roles and needs) → Data Agent (tables, columns, relationships) → Solution Agent (apps, flows, Power Pages sites, agents). At each stage choose Looks good, or Edit inline or through Copilot, then Keep or Review.
Save and createSave tables > solution name (letters, numbers, underscores) > publisher or existing solution; the plan is stored in the solution (Objects view). Then Create per tile: canvas (responsive screens per table), model-driven (modern app designer), Power Pages (needs System Administrator and permission to register a Microsoft Entra app), cloud flow (prefilled natural-language prompt), agent (prefilled name, description, instructions, plan tables as knowledge). Save and publish before use.
CollaborateUp to 100 authors in copresence, one editor (the first in). Share as Viewer or Co-Owner. The admin setting Enable plan level security roles for plan designer is Off by default.
From a solutionSolutions > Create plan from a solution: needs at least one app and one associated table; not recommended for the default solution. Unmanaged: the plan is saved in the same solution. Managed: saved in a new unmanaged solution.

Code-app generation from a plan and Power Apps vibe are Preview.

Exam traps
  • The plan agents are design-time helpers, not Copilot Studio agents. Nothing is created until Save tables and Create.
  • Order is fixed: Requirement, then Data, then Solution. The Solution Agent proposes technologies; the Data Agent designs the tables.
  • Existing apps added with Replace or Add technology aren't added to the new solution.
  • Model-driven apps use Dataverse only; one screen merging several non-Dataverse systems points to a canvas app. Power Pages serves external users.

Evaluate built-in agents to include in the business solution

Think of the built-in options as four families: managed agents in Copilot Studio, Power Apps built-in skills in model-driven apps, the Document Processing Agent and web agents in Power Pages. Judge each on fit, license, admin switches, GA or Preview status and environment. Building them is covered in §1.2, §2.1 and §3.2.

OptionWhat it does and what it needs
Managed agentsPrebuilt, complete agent solutions. Copilot Studio > Agents > Install a managed agent > Install > Open. Specialize with add-ons: agent Overview > Customize > Install (authenticate flagged connections). Add-on contents can't be modified; assess safety and legal fit yourself.
Data entry (AI form fill assistance)Suggests values for blank fields from usage, pasted text or images (smart paste) and uploaded files (Files); saved only when accepted. Needs the new look, an AI form fill assistance setting on and the Allow form fill assistance column property. Default is on for Dynamics 365 model-driven apps but off for Power Apps ones. Generally available in Dynamics 365 apps; Preview (production-ready) in Power Apps.
Data explorationType a question to filter, sort and text-search a view (two words or fewer run a plain text search). The Visualize chart option is Preview on the admin settings page. Hidden without a qualifying license: Power Apps premium or Dynamics 365 Enterprise or Premium (the admin page words this differently for Power Apps-only environments).
Summary (row summary)Per-table prompt (Tables > table > Customizations > Row summary > Prompt > Test prompt > Apply to main forms), shown in the collapsible insights bar of main forms and the inline Summary action in views. Needs Row summaries enabled under Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Summary (the same control is also shown as the AI insight cards feature setting, default On; that location will be removed in a future release); not offered for Case, Lead and Opportunity.
Document Processing AgentMonitors incoming documents, validates them against rules, controls routing. The archived 2025 wave 1 release plan lists public preview on May 15, 2025 and no GA date Preview. Alternative: AI Builder plus Power Automate.
Power Pages agentsAdd from the set up workspace (answers from site information) or Start from a form Preview; extend with a Copilot Studio agent, Bing search or Omnichannel handoff.

Process lives in Dynamics 365Its own agents: Sales Qualification, Opportunity, Research and Recommended Actions (the Sales Close Agent can't be created from September 30, 2026 and existing instances are removed on October 30, 2026; the Sales Development agent Preview replaces it); Customer Service Customer Intent, Case Management and Customer Knowledge Management
  • Prerequisites: Copilot enabled for the tenant and environment, the new look, and each feature's own setting; primary controls are moving to the admin center under Copilot > Settings > Power Apps (Data entry, Data exploration, Summary). The features above check for Power Apps premium or Dynamics 365 licenses, so confirm any Copilot Studio licensing requirement for the specific agent you plan to use.
  • Environment: deploy production agents in a non-default production environment. The environment's Generative AI features card holds separate checkboxes for Move data across regions (hidden for U.S. and government cloud), Bing search and Microsoft 365 services.
Exam traps
  • Do not rely on a count of built-in skills: the live AI features overview lists exactly three (Data entry, Data exploration, Summary). Learn the named skills rather than a number.
  • The managed-agent catalog is under Install a managed agent on the Copilot Studio Agents page.
  • Form fill Default is on for Dynamics 365 apps and off for Power Apps apps, so "Copilot is on but nothing appears" is often this setting or a missing column property.
  • Data exploration finds rows; a row summary summarizes one. Document Processing Agent, agent feed, Power Pages agent from a form and the Visualize chart are Preview.

Recommend extensibility options

Microsoft's "no cliffs" principle: if a built-in capability falls short, a supported extension exists, and extensions reach low-code makers as connectors, components and plug-ins. Know when an extension is needed, what kind, and who builds it.

Full control of agent orchestrationMicrosoft 365 Agents SDK, deployable through Copilot StudioDeveloper
Application without an APIDesktop flowMaker
  • Custom connector: wraps a REST API (SOAP only in Logic Apps); authentication is generic OAuth 2.0, service-specific OAuth 2.0, Basic or API key, with Microsoft Entra ID recommended; private APIs are reached through an on-premises data gateway.
  • PCF isn't supported on-premises, and a code component that calls external services directly (declared with <external-service-usage>) makes the app premium. Code components aren't supported inside component libraries.
  • User-defined function syntax (parameters and result are typed; custom types use :=):
LibraryType := Type( [ { Title: Text, Author: Text, Genre: Text } ] );
LibraryGenre( SelectedGenre: Text ): LibraryType = Filter( Library, Genre = SelectedGenre );
Exam traps
  • Custom connector (built once, reused everywhere) versus REST API tool (one agent, one-off, Preview) versus MCP tool (MCP-compatible service, Streamable only).
  • Component library (canvas components made by makers) versus PCF (developer code); a library can't hold code components.
  • Plug-in runs automatically on a Dataverse event for every channel; a custom API is a named operation callers invoke, and its plug-in is optional.
  • "Instant low-code plug-ins" is the old name of Functions in Dataverse (Preview). When a platform feature already fits, recommend it over custom code.

Recommend environment types

TypePurpose and facts to remember
ProductionPermanent work. Created by an admin or anyone with a Power Apps license when 1 GB of database capacity is free. Can't be reset.
DefaultOne per tenant, "{tenant} (default)"; experimentation only, no backup guarantees. Every licensed user is a maker, no one is auto-admin. Can't be deleted or manually backed up; 3 GB database, 3 GB file and 1 GB log included; 1 TB limit.
SandboxNon-production development and testing with copy and reset (only sandboxes can be reset; a reset deletes apps, flows, custom connectors and connections). Administration mode admits only System Administrator and System Customizer. Converting production to sandbox can't be blocked.
DeveloperPersonal workspace for its owner; no security groups. Unmanaged ones are Deprecated: none created from November 15, 2026, existing ones suspended from December 15, 2026; only managed developer environments remain, one per user.
Trial (standard)30 days, then disabled and deleted; one per user; uses no paid capacity; convert to production to keep it. In Copilot Studio, expiry deletes its agents.
Trial (subscription-based)Larger multiuser proof of concept that tenant admins add in the admin center; lasts as long as the admin-managed subscription (its end date can be extended); Dataverse mandatory.
Dataverse for TeamsDeprecated: none created from November 15, 2026; environments not upgraded are suspended September 15, 2027 and decommissioned October 30, 2027.
  • Roles: Environment Admin and Environment Maker; neither grants access to the environment's data.
  • Managed Environments: premium governance for any type (environment groups, limit sharing, usage insights, data policies, pipelines, solution checker enforcement, routing and more). Included with standalone Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot Studio, Power Pages and Dynamics 365 licenses, not the Developer Plan. Enable under Manage > Environments > Enable Managed Environments as Power Platform or Dynamics 365 Administrator (Environment Admin can't). Production, sandbox and trial need Dataverse.
  • Environment groups: "folders" of managed environments; one group each, no overlap or nesting, regions may differ. Published rules lock settings in every member; no per-environment exceptions.
  • Environment routing: tenant setting (Manage > Tenant settings > Environment routing), off by default, Power Platform admins only. Makers opening Copilot Studio, Power Apps or Power Automate land in a personal, managed developer environment, become admins there and join an environment group; rules are evaluated by priority.
  • ALM layout: development and production at minimum, plus at least one test environment (UAT, SIT or training if needed). A solution imports into a newer environment but not reliably into an older one, so keep development in the same or an earlier service-update station than production.
Exam traps
  • A managed environment (governance) is not a managed solution (deployment package).
  • Only sandbox environments can be reset; production, trial and default can't, and default can't even be deleted.
  • Standard trial: 30 days, one per user, self-service. Subscription-based trial: admin-managed, multiuser, lasts as long as the subscription.
  • The Developer environment type isn't the Developer Plan. Unmanaged developer environments and Dataverse for Teams are deprecated, though older material still presents them as the normal maker sandbox.
  • Environment groups accept managed environments only, and an environment belongs to only one group.

Apply a Microsoft Power Platform solution and ALM strategy

Solutions implement ALM. They carry components (tables, apps, flows, agents, prompts, plug-ins) and configuration, never Dataverse data, and can be up to 95 MB. Use your own publisher, build in unmanaged solutions in development and deploy managed solutions everywhere else.

UnmanagedManaged
WhereDevelopment; the source you keep in source controlAny environment that isn't the solution's development environment (test, UAT, production)
Edit and exportEditable; export as unmanaged or managed (a build artifact)Components can't be edited directly and the solution can't be exported
DeleteRemoves only the container; customizations stayUninstalls everything, including data in its custom tables and columns
Import rule-Can't be imported into the environment that holds its source unmanaged solution
  • Layers and defaults: unmanaged customizations sit on top and the top layer wins, except that model-driven apps, forms and site maps merge. New objects go to the Common Data Services Default Solution unless you work inside an unmanaged solution; the Default Solution can't be exported. A preferred solution (Solutions > select > Set preferred solution) receives new objects instead.
Import actionBehaviorUse when
Upgrade (default)Rolls up patches and deletes components missing from the new versionStandard release; a column, form or flow must disappear
Stage for UpgradeInstalls the new version but defers deletion until Apply Solution UpgradeOld and new needed side by side for data migration
UpdateReplaces the solution; removed components are not deleted; typically fastestQuick change where leftovers are acceptable
PatchOnly changes to a parent managed solution, layered on top; can't delete. Learn says using patches isn't recommendedSmall hotfix

The version format is major.minor.build.revision and each update needs a higher number.

Environment variableConnection reference
HoldsA parameter value (such as a SharePoint site and list) used by apps, flows and plug-insA pointer to a connection for one connector
DetailTypes: Decimal number, Text, JSON, Two options, Data source, Secret (Azure Key Vault). Current Value wins over Default ValueFlows use it for all connectors; canvas apps only for non-OAuth, implicitly shared connections. Import prompts for a connection per reference so flows turn on
ALM ruleShip the definition, set the value per environmentSupply a connection per environment; import custom connectors first
  • Solution checker enforcement (managed environment > Edit Managed Environments): None; Warn (import continues, summary email); Block (highly critical issues cancel the import before any change). Unavailable in administration mode.
  • Block unmanaged customizations (setting, default Off) blocks importing unmanaged solutions, creating components and editing managed ones; environment variable changes and exporting unmanaged solutions stay allowed.
Deployment optionUse when
PipelinesGoverned, in-product, maker-friendly promotion with preflight validation and connections and environment variables supplied up front
Dataverse Git integrationSource control from developer environments (Azure DevOps or GitHub), not test or production; build artifacts, then deploy with pipelines
Azure DevOps or GitHub automationFull CI/CD, or a different tenant (pipelines can't cross tenants)
  • Pipelines deploy solutions plus connections, connection references and environment variables, not data. Default import is Upgrade without Overwrite customizations. One artifact moves through the stages in order (no QA bypass). A pipeline is visible only from an unmanaged solution in a linked development environment.
  • Host = storage and run history (a dedicated production environment is recommended; it can't also be the development environment; deleting it deletes all pipelines). Targets must be managed; host and development needn't be; all need Dataverse. From October 2026 admins have 30 days (plus one 30-day extension) to approve Managed Environments for unmanaged targets or deployments are blocked; or enable automatic conversion (Deployments > Settings).
  • Platform host (created in the tenant's home region on first use): personal pipelines, one development and two targets, not shareable or extendable; default, Teams and no-Dataverse environments can't be targets. Custom host (Deployments > New custom host): three environments minimum, four recommended, up to seven stages, shareable and extendable.
AI assetALM behavior
PlanStored in its main solution; adding tables or apps associates other solutions; packaging its components in one solution lets you deploy them as managed
Cloud flows, canvas appsSolution-aware; flows bind to connection references
Copilot Studio agentAdd to a custom unmanaged solution (Add existing > Agent) and run Add required objects; needs System Customizer; a managed solution can't be exported. Custom topics and knowledge may be missing; a topic name with a period blocks export. Import custom connectors first, then configure authentication again and publish before sharing
Prompt (AI model)Add existing > AI models; deploy as managed from development or a sandbox; don't edit after import (set Allow customizations off in Managed Properties); if edited, delete the imported solution and import again
Row summaryAdd existing > More > Other > AI Skill Config (not rows owned by System)
  1. Run a pipeline: choose the development environment → Solutions, open an unmanaged solution → Pipelines (or Overview > Deploy) → select the stage and Deploy here → Now or Later, then Next (preflight checks) → supply connection references and environment variables → review and Deploy. Stages run in order.
  2. Upgrade a managed solution: raise the version, export as managed, import, choose Upgrade, Stage for Upgrade or Update; if staged, select the base solution and Apply Solution Upgrade.
Exam traps
  • Update keeps components removed in development; only Upgrade (the default) deletes them, and patches can't delete anything. Stage for Upgrade isn't finished until Apply Solution Upgrade.
  • A managed solution can't be exported or imported beside its source unmanaged solution, and deleting it loses data in its custom tables and columns.
  • An environment variable carries a parameter value; a connection reference carries a connection. Ship the definition and set the value in each environment.
  • Pipelines run only from an unmanaged solution in a linked development environment, deploy managed solutions to managed targets, can't use the host as the development environment and can't cross tenants.
  • An imported agent isn't ready until authentication is reconfigured and it is published; export from a custom unmanaged solution and import custom connectors first.

sections.title: 1.2 Build data models
sections.html:
Skills measured: create and edit tables in the data workspace • create and modify standard tables • configure table properties • create and modify columns • configure table relationships • configure prompt columns • configure row summaries • configure public views • configure main forms • configure security. Build one small model end to end in a trial environment: Copilot-generated tables, a custom table with an autonumber column, a 1:N relationship with Restrict Delete, a prompt column, a row summary, a role-based main form and a column security profile.

Create and edit tables in the data workspace

The data workspace is the Power Apps experience in which you create tables, configure table relationships and view a diagram of your data (also called the visual table designer). Open it at make.powerapps.com with Tables > New table > Create new tables. GA (announced October 2024). The page Choose an option to create tables offers four starting points:

OptionUse it when / what to remember
Start with CopilotYou can describe several related tables in natural language. The Table options menu sets the number of tables, the table size and whether relationships are included; refine in the Copilot panel and finish with Save and exit. Copilot must be enabled for the environment (on by default).
Excel or .CSVThe data already sits in a spreadsheet (New table > Create with external data > File > Edit column > Create). The preview shows only the first 20 rows; the full dataset is ingested after you save. Only the first range of the first tab is converted.
SharePoint list PreviewImports a SharePoint list as a table; Learn labels this option (preview).
Start from blankAn empty table that you define yourself.

The same New table menu also holds Set advanced properties (a blank table plus an Advanced options area for settings such as track changes and audit changes), Create with external data and Create a virtual table.

  • Canvas commands: Back, New table, Existing table, Hide/View data, Create relationships (select one table, Ctrl+click a second, then select the command) and Remove. A table's menu offers Row ownership (user or team, or organization), Properties and Remove.
  • Remove deletes a new table together with its rows; on an existing table it only removes the table from the diagram and deletes no data.
  • Not supported in the workspace: columns of type Rich text, Customer, Autonumber and Formula, many-to-many relationships and relationships between two existing tables. Create those from the table's Columns and Relationships areas.
  • Who can build: a Dataverse environment, the System Customizer security role, and a role with Create, Read and Write privileges on the Entity table. Environment Maker alone has no Dataverse data privileges.
Start tableTarget tableOne-to-manyMany-to-oneMany-to-many
NewNewYesYesNo
ExistingNewYesNoNo
ExistingExistingNoNoNo

Decision rules. Several related tables from a description, with a diagram: Start with Copilot. Data already in a workbook: Excel or .CSV (the uploaded file stays in the File Upload table). Live external data that must not be copied: a virtual table. Autonumber, formula, N:N or existing-to-existing links: leave the workspace. Copilot sequence: Tables > New table > Create new tables > Start with Copilot > describe the tables (adjust Table options) > iterate in the Copilot panel > Save and exit.

Exam traps
  • The Power Pages Data workspace (make.powerpages.microsoft.com > site > Edit > Data) is a different tool; elastic tables are unsupported there. The per-table table designer (table > Edit) is also not the data workspace.
  • Existing-to-new works only as one-to-many. Many-to-one from an existing table, and any many-to-many, must be created in the table's Relationships area.
  • The Excel preview shows 20 rows, but all rows are loaded after saving.
  • Remove never deletes data when the table already existed.

Create and modify standard tables

"Standard" is used in two ways. As a category, standard tables are the out-of-box tables (Account, Contact, Task, User and so on) listed on the Recommended tab of Tables; the Custom tab lists tables that makers created. As a table type, Standard is the default type, next to Activity, Virtual and Elastic. The type is chosen when the table is created and can't be changed afterwards.

Table typeChoose it whenKey restrictions
StandardMost business data that needs relationships, joins, security and transactions.Default; full feature set.
ActivityCalendar-style items with start/end, due date or duration that users open, cancel or complete.User or team ownership only; primary column is Subject.
VirtualExternal data that you read at run time without copying it.Organization-owned only; no auditing, change tracking or column security; an existing table can't be converted.
ElasticVery large, high-volume or changing-schema data, with automatic row expiry (time to live).Azure Cosmos DB; no multi-row transactions, cascading behavior, or calculated and rollup columns.

Modify before you build. Reuse an out-of-box table and rename or add columns before you create a custom table. Standard tables can't be deleted, but you can hide them by removing their privileges from security roles. Edits to managed tables are limited by managed properties. Only custom tables outside managed solutions can be deleted, by a System Administrator, and the data is lost (recover from a backup).

Table segmentation. When you add an existing table to a solution (Solutions > Add existing > Table) you choose what to include:

OptionWhat is added
No objects selected (default)Only the table's friendly name: no metadata and no components.
Edit objectsOnly the components you tick: columns, relationships, business rules, views, forms, charts.
Include table metadataTable properties (auditing, duplicate detection, change tracking) but no components.
Include all objectsAll components and metadata. Can't be undone; use it only for an unmanaged table that does not exist in the target environment (a new custom table needs it, or the import fails with a missing dependency).

The system auto-selects Include all objects for an unmanaged table and Include table metadata when the table has an unmanaged layer. A customized Quick Find view pulls its required columns into the solution whatever segmentation option you pick.

Exam traps
  • Standard table (category) is not the same thing as Type = Standard.
  • To ship one new column and one form change on Account, choose Edit objects. Include all objects adds unrelated components and can make downstream customizations inactive.
  • No objects selected is the default, but it carries no components.
  • You can't convert a Standard table to Elastic or Virtual later; the type is fixed at creation.

Configure table properties

Edit properties under Tables > select the table > Properties > Advanced options; at creation use New table > Set advanced properties. In a solution the classic table editor uses Settings.

PropertyWhat it doesChange after creation?
Display name, Plural display nameLabels shown in apps.Yes
Schema nameSystem name, publisher prefix plus a name without spaces.No
TypeStandard, Activity, Virtual or Elastic.No
Record ownershipUser or team, or Organization (a Filtered option is Preview).No
Notes (Enable attachments), Activities (Creating a new activity), Business process flows, Connections (Can have connections), Feedback (Can be linked to feedback), Queues (Can be added to a queue), Sending email (Can have a contact email)Turn on the matching feature for the table.Enable only; can't be turned off
Track changesDetects what changed since the last sync, for efficient data synchronization.Yes
Audit changes to its dataRecords changes to rows; needs auditing turned on for the environment.Yes
Leverage quick create form if availableLets the Create button open a published quick create form.Yes
Duplicate detection, Mail merge, Document management, Access teams, Color, Custom helpOptional features and presentation.Yes
  • Ownership: User or team gives row-level security with Assign and Share privileges and every access level. Organization is all-or-nothing: users have access to all rows or none, and the access levels are only None or Organization. Activity tables are always user or team owned.
  • Primary column defaults: display name Name, requirement Business required, maximum length 100. Activity tables use Subject instead. An Elastic table gets an automatic time-to-live column (seconds).
  • Auditing works at three levels: environment, table and column. Table-level auditing needs the environment level; column-level auditing needs both. System Administrator or System Customizer can configure it.
  • Primary image: system tables that support images already have an Image column; on a custom table create an Image column first, then select it.

Decision rules. Users must see only their own rows: User or team ownership (decide before you build). Reference data everyone shares: Organization. Incremental sync to another system: Track changes. Prove who changed a value: environment auditing plus table auditing plus the column's audit setting. Attachments or queues likely later: enable them at creation, because they can't be disabled.

Exam traps
  • Track changes (sync) is not Auditing (history of who changed what).
  • Schema name, Type and Record ownership are locked; the display name is not.
  • Enable-only options are one-way. Auditing, Track changes, quick create and duplicate detection can be toggled at any time.
  • An organization-owned table can't use User or Business Unit access levels or Assign/Share.

Create and modify columns

Open Tables > table > Columns > New column, set Display name, Data type, Format, Behavior (Simple, Calculated or Rollup), Required level (Optional, Business Recommended, Business Required) and Searchable, select Done, then Save table; nothing exists until you save the table. After the column is saved you can't change the Name or the Data type, with one exception: a Text column can be converted to Autonumber (and autonumber can be turned off again by choosing a different data type). The display name stays editable.

Data typeFacts to remember
Text / Text area / Multiline textMaximum 4,000 / 4,000 / 1,048,576 characters (defaults 100 / 100 / 150).
AutonumberShown as a data type under Text. Types: String prefixed number, Date prefixed number, Custom. Default seed 1000; the seed isn't carried by a solution. Create it from Tables > Columns, not in the classic solution explorer or the data workspace.
Whole numberFormats None, Duration, Time zone, Language (formats, not separate types).
Decimal / FloatDecimal up to 10 decimal places, exact; Float up to 5, approximate.
CurrencyAdds a Currency lookup, an Exchange Rate and a base-currency (_Base) column.
Date and Time / Date OnlyStored in UTC. Behavior: User local (converted per user; default for new Date and Time columns), Time zone independent, Date only (Date Only type; no time zone conversion; birthdays and anniversaries).
Choice / ChoicesLocal or global choice sets. Multi-select Choices can't be used in business rules, rollup or calculated columns.
Yes/NoTwo options with custom labels.
LookupCreates a many-to-one relationship. Anyone who can read the row sees the related row's primary column value, so keep secrets out of primary columns.
File / ImageOne primary image per table; a custom table needs an Image column before it can show a primary image.
Formula / Calculated / RollupPower Fx on read (formula column, up to 1,000 characters), real-time expression, or aggregate of related rows: see §3.3.
PromptAI-generated, stored value: see the prompt column topic below.

Decision rules. Money in several currencies: Currency. Exact equality or reporting: Decimal; approximate range comparisons: Float. Local business time: Date and Time with User local. A date that must read the same everywhere: Date Only with Date only behavior. Small fixed list: Choice; several selections: Choices; a growing or shared list: a table plus a Lookup. Generated reference such as INV-1000: Autonumber. Per-row AI text: Prompt column.

Exam traps
  • The data type is permanent (turning a Text column into Autonumber, or autonumber back off, is the only conversion), but the display name can be edited.
  • Duration, Time zone and Language are formats of Whole number, not data types.
  • A Date and Time column using the Date only format with User local behavior still converts between time zones.
  • Autonumber and Formula columns can't be created in the data workspace. Deleting a column needs the System Administrator role.

Configure table relationships

Only two relationship types exist: one-to-many (1:N) and many-to-many (N:N). Many-to-one is the same 1:N relationship seen from the child, and the lookup column always sits on the many (child) table. Creating a lookup column creates a many-to-one relationship. Create one under Tables > table > Relationships > New relationship (some pages say Add relationship), choose Many-to-one, One-to-many or Many-to-many, pick the Related table, select Done, then Save table. For a one-to-many the lookup is created on the related table; to put it on the current table, create a many-to-one instead.

  • N:N uses a hidden relationship (intersect) table that can't have custom columns and is never visible. To associate rows the user needs Append privilege on both tables.
  • Deleting a 1:N removes its lookup column; a relationship with dependencies (for example the lookup on a form) can't be deleted until the dependency is removed.
  • Advanced options on 1:N: navigation (Do not display, Use custom label, Use plural name; display area and order) and the relationship behavior.
Behavior (UI name)Assign, Reparent, Share, UnshareDeleteMerge, Rollup view
ParentalCascade AllCascade AllCascade None
Referential, Remove LinkCascade NoneRemove LinkCascade None
Referential, Restrict DeleteCascade NoneRestrictCascade None
Custom (classic name: Configurable Cascading)You choose a behavior for each action.

Options per action: Assign, Reparent, Share, Unshare and Rollup view: Cascade All, Cascade Active, Cascade User-owned, Cascade None. Delete: Cascade All, Remove Link, Restrict. Merge: Cascade All or Cascade None. Cascade Active acts on active child rows; Cascade User-owned acts on child rows owned by the same user as the parent row; Remove Link clears the lookup; Restrict blocks deleting the parent while child rows exist. A custom table can't be the primary table in a cascading relationship with a system table.

Decision rules. Children must die or follow the parent: Parental. Delete the parent but keep the children: Referential, Remove Link. Never orphan children: Referential, Restrict Delete. Reassign only open child rows: Custom with Assign set to Cascade Active. Peers with no parent: N:N.

Exam traps
  • Custom and Configurable Cascading are the same option under two names.
  • Delete offers only Cascade All, Remove Link and Restrict; Merge offers only Cascade All and Cascade None.
  • Parental also cascades Assign, Share, Unshare and Reparent, not only Delete.
  • N:1 is not a separate stored relationship type, and a N:N table has no custom columns.

Configure prompt columns

A prompt column is an AI-powered Dataverse data type: a natural-language prompt over other columns of the same table whose generated result is stored in the table persistently, ready for apps, flows or reports. GA since May 4, 2026 per the Dataverse release plan; the Learn page shows no preview banner. Prerequisites: the same licensing as AI Builder prompts, the Copilot and AI prompts features on for the environment, and the Block unmanaged customizations setting off (the error names msdyn_AIConfiguration).

  1. Power Apps > Tables > open the table > New > Column.
  2. Enter a display name and description; set Data type to Prompt; clear Allow form fill assistance.
  3. Select + Add new prompt (up to five prompt columns per table) and write the prompt.
  4. Select + Add content > table > column > Add for each input column. Formula, file, image and other prompt columns are ignored as inputs.
  5. Select Test (free), then Save on the prompt page and Save on the column.
  • The required text input variable PromptColumnRecordId filters on the primary column; the column can't be saved without it.
  • When it runs: when a row is created or when a column referenced by the prompt is updated, asynchronously. If no referenced column changes, it doesn't run and uses no credits. Existing rows aren't processed by default; an opt-in bulk backfill exists but is still rolling out (turn on the environment setting Allow bulk processing of existing records, which is off by default, then select Also generate values for Existing records in bulk and Run prompt; the job runs under System jobs). On-demand execution without updating a row isn't supported, so editing the prompt doesn't recalculate old rows.
  • Filter conditions (Apply filter > Add filter) limit execution to matching rows. Clearing Allow prompt column execution turns generation off.
  • Two helper columns, <column>_PromptColumnStatus and <column>_PromptColumnDetails, report status: 0 NotStarted, 1 InProgress, 2 Completed, 2000 skipped because the filter wasn't met, 2001 skipped because no input column was updated, 3 Failed.
  • Cost: AI Builder credits are consumed first, then Copilot Credits. AI Builder credits are being phased out (end of sales 2025-11-01, end of life 2026-11-01), and AI Builder features continue on Copilot Credits. Review usage in Power Automate > Automation center > AI Builder activity.
  • Security: prompt columns aren't audited. A failure can come from missing permission on an input column or from lack of credits. Secure both the input column and the prompt column.
Prompt columnRow summaryFormula column
ResultGenerative AI text, storedCopilot text on a form or view, not storedPower Fx value, evaluated on read
TriggerRow create or referenced-column updateWhen the user views the rowEvery read
CostCreditsNeeds an eligible licenseNone
Exam traps
  • Stored AI value that apps and flows can use: prompt column. A row summary is generated on demand and isn't stored.
  • Status 2000 (filter not met) and 2001 (no input updated) both mean "completed but skipped", not failed.
  • The limit is five prompt columns per table, and a column that reads a secured column leaks data unless it is secured too.

Configure row summaries

A row summary is a Copilot-generated overview of a row. It appears in a collapsible summary bar at the top of main forms and, per row, from views. It is generated on demand and isn't stored. The table configuration applies to all main forms and views of that table. A Power Platform administrator must enable Row summaries for the environment (Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Summary). The same control is also known as AI insight cards (app setting EnableFormInsights); Learn calls the Copilot settings the preferred location and says the AI insight cards location will be removed in a future release.

  1. Sign in to make.powerapps.com, select Tables and open the table. It must contain at least one row, or the command stays disabled.
  2. Under Customizations, select Row summary.
  3. In the Prompt box add columns with Add or by typing /, and add formatting and language instructions.
  4. Select Test prompt; it uses the most recently edited row.
  5. Select Apply to main forms.
  • Edit or hide: open the table and choose Row summary (applied); clear Show row summary to hide it. Forms that carry a summary show an AI icon in the forms list.
  • Language: include the LanguageCode input and the instruction "You must respond in language <LanguageCode>." New summaries get it by default; add it manually to older ones. Unsupported languages fall back to English; without the instruction the summary uses the prompt's own language.
  • Not available for Case, Lead and Opportunity, which have their own Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Sales summaries.
  • Limits: no arithmetic on column values, no date-based logic (use calculated columns or business logic), related-record links may not render, formula or calculated values can be inaccurate.
  • ALM: each summary is a row in the AI Skill Config table. Add it to a solution with Add existing > More > Other > AI Skill Config, and never add rows owned by System.
  • License: Power Apps premium for model-driven apps in Power Apps, or Dynamics 365 enterprise or premium; users without it don't see the summary. The Learn pages show no preview label.
Exam traps
  • Row summary is disabled on an empty table, not broken.
  • The setting that must be on is Row summaries (Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Summary); AI insight cards is the older name of the same control.
  • The summary is configured on the table and applies to every main form and view, not to a single form.
  • Row summary (read-only recap, not stored) and prompt column (stored, usable in views and flows) are different features.

Configure public views

View typeWhat it is
PublicGeneral-purpose view for everyone; usable in subgrids and dashboards. Views you create in make.powerapps.com are public views. A new custom table gets Active and Inactive public views.
SystemViews the app depends on: Quick Find, Advanced Find, Associated and Lookup. They can't be deleted or deactivated. The Quick Find view defines the searched (find) columns.
PersonalCreated by an individual user for their own use.
  1. Solutions > open the solution > Tables > the table > Views > Add view (name, description) > Create, or open an existing view.
  2. Add columns with + View column or drag them from Table columns; use the Related tab for columns of a related table. The column header menu offers Remove, Move left or right, width, Sort A to Z or Z to A and Filter by.
  3. Sort with Sort by and Then sort by; build richer conditions with Edit filters: Add row, Add group (And or Or) or Add related table (supports only Contains data).
  4. Select Save and publish. To change the default: Views > More commands > Set as default view.

Role-based public views. Set the organization setting EnableRoleBasedSystemViews to true (OrganizationSettingsEditor tool; effective immediately). Then open Views, select a non-default public view, choose View settings > Specific security roles, pick roles and Save and Publish. The role list comes from the root business unit. The setting filters only the view selector of the table list: subgrids still show system and associated views, and data access is still decided by security role privileges. Changing back to Everyone can take up to 24 hours. The model-driven views article still links this topic with a "(preview)" label, but the Power Platform release plan lists role-based system views as generally available since August 30, 2025.

Decision rules. Same filtered list for everyone: public view. Personal slice: personal view. Change what Quick Find searches: edit the Quick Find view (find columns need the classic view designer). Show a view only to some roles: View settings. Make a different view open first: Set as default view. Forms and views for model-driven apps are covered again in §2.1.

Exam traps
  • A default public view can't be assigned security roles; make another view the default first.
  • Role-based view access hides a view from the selector; it doesn't secure the rows.
  • Filters on a related table support only Contains data.
  • The access article says "public system views": it means views of type Public, the only ones that can be role-managed. Quick Find, Advanced Find, Associated and Lookup are separate system view types.

Configure main forms

Form typePurposeRoles and fallback
MainPrimary data-entry form built from tabs, sections and columns or components; the default form is named Information.Can be assigned to roles; can be a fallback form
Quick CreateFast creation in a side panel; needs a published form and the table property Leverage quick create form if available.Form order only
Quick ViewRead-only data of a lookup's related row, embedded in another form.Form order only
CardCompact form for views and mobile.Form order only

Create a form under Tables > table > Forms > New form, choose the type, then Edit and use Save only or Save and Publish. The designer panes are Columns, Components, Tree view and Form libraries. Copilot can suggest columns, but only for new Quick view and Quick create forms. A generative page can be added from Components > Display > Generative page (see §2.1).

Form settings (from the Forms area or the designer command bar) has four areas:

  • Security role: Everyone or Specific security roles; then Save and Publish. Only main forms can be role-assigned.
  • Form order: pick the form set (Main, Quick Create, Quick View, Card) and drag forms; the order decides which form is shown by default. It is not a security control.
  • Fallback forms: main forms only; shown to users whose roles match no assigned form. When forms are assigned to roles, at least one fallback form is required. Strategies: one form for everyone (no fallback needed), a contingency form with minimal data (assign only System Administrator), or a generic form that is the least specialized, shown to everyone and last in the order.
  • Form access checker: lets you verify how users access forms.
  • Performance: the first expanded (default) tab initializes all its controls when the form loads. Keep quick view, subgrid and timeline controls off it. Default Max Width is 1900.
  • AI form fill assistance: main and quick create forms; GA in Dynamics 365 apps, production-ready Preview in Power Apps; the column property is labelled Allow form fill assistance (preview); not applied to columns with column security. Admin path: Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data entry.
Exam traps
  • Quick create, quick view and card forms can't be assigned to security roles, and fallback applies only to main forms.
  • Form order chooses the default form; security roles decide who may open a form.
  • Row summary and AI form fill assistance have different admin paths (Summary versus Data entry).
  • Quick create fails to appear on the Create button unless both the form and the table property are set.

Configure security

Who builds. Creating tables needs the System Customizer role plus Create, Read and Write privileges on the Entity table. Environment Maker has no Dataverse data privileges. Creating or editing security roles and deleting tables or columns needs System Administrator. Power Platform and Dynamics 365 administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID don't give Dataverse data access; add System Administrator in the environment. Predefined roles can't be edited, so copy System Administrator when you need a custom role.

Access levelUsers can access
NoneNo rows.
UserRows they own, rows shared with them, and rows shared with a team they belong to.
Business UnitRows in their business unit (includes User).
Parent: Child Business UnitRows in their business unit and every business unit below it (includes Business Unit and User).
OrganizationAll rows, whatever the business unit.
  • Table privileges: Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append To, Assign, Share. Append attaches this row to another; Append To lets another row be attached to this one. Privileges from several roles are cumulative: the broadest wins.
  • Create a role: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > the environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > + New role. Member's privilege inheritance: Team privileges only or Direct User (Basic) access level and Team privileges (default).
  • Business units: one root business unit that can't be deleted; each user belongs to exactly one business unit; each business unit has a default team. Teams: Owner teams can own rows and hold roles; Access teams own no rows and hold no roles (rows are shared to them); Microsoft Entra group teams can own rows and hold roles.
  • Sharing is the exception mechanism; share with a team instead of many users.
  • Hierarchy security is off by default. Manager or Position model; direct reports get Read, Write, Append, Append To, indirect reports are read-only; the manager needs at least User-level Read.
  • Preview Filtered record ownership limits rows by a column value (for example City) without an owner.

Column-level security. Needs the System Administrator role, which is never restricted by it.

  1. make.powerapps.com > Solutions > the unmanaged solution > table > Schema > Columns > the column > Advanced options > Enable column security > Save.
  2. Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Column security profiles > New Profile.
  3. On the Teams or Users tab add the people who need access.
  4. On the Column Permission tab select the columns > Edit > set Read, Read unmasked, Update and Create.

Without a profile only system administrators can use a secured column (others see a lock and asterisks). Lookup columns, formula columns, primary name columns, system columns (for example createdon, statecode) and columns of virtual tables can't be secured. Secure calculated and prompt columns that read a secured column. Changes need a browser refresh to take effect.

Decision rules. A regional manager over child business units: Parent: Child Business Unit. Division B must not see Division A rows: separate business units with business-unit-level roles. HR-only salary: column security plus an HR profile, tested with a non-admin account. Cross-table append for N:N: Append on both tables.

Exam traps
  • A tenant admin role does not grant Dataverse data access.
  • Access teams hold no security roles and own no rows.
  • Lookup, formula and primary name columns can't be secured, and System Administrators always see the data.
  • Roles on forms and public views only change what is shown; table privileges still decide data access.

Sources: Create and edit tables (data workspace) · Types of tables · Edit tables · Table segmentation · Create and edit columns · Types of columns · Autonumber columns · Lookup relationships · 1:N relationships and behavior · Prompt columns · Row summary · Manage access to public views · Control access to forms · Security roles and privileges · Column-level security
