sections.title: 2.1 Create model-driven apps
sections.html:
Skills measured: Create and configure forms for model-driven apps • Create and configure views for model-driven apps • Create generative pages by using natural language • Compose a model-driven app • Configure access to forms and views for model-driven apps • Configure access to model-driven apps • Create and configure model-driven app charts and dashboards. Practise by building one small app in an unmanaged solution: two role-based main forms, a view limited to one app, a generative page, a dashboard with a system chart and a role-based share. Table design, columns and the underlying security model are in §1.2; business rules and process logic are in §3.3.

Create and configure forms for model-driven apps

Forms are built in the modern form designer: Solutions > your solution > the table > Forms > New form (choose the type, enter a name, Create), or select an existing form. The designer has a command bar (Save, Publish, Undo, Redo), a live preview, and panes for Columns, Components, Tree view and Form libraries. Changes reach users only after Save and publish.

Form typePurposeRules to rememberAssign to roles?
MainFull record form with tabs, sections, subgrids and componentsEach table needs a fallback form, which is a main form shown to users whose roles have no form assigned. A main form can be set Inactive.Yes
Quick createShort data entry from the global Create button or + New on a lookup or subgridThe table needs Enable quick create forms. Always one section with three columns. No subgrids, quick view forms, web resources, iFrames, notes or Bing Maps. Business rules and form scripts are supported.No
Quick viewRead-only data of a related row, shown on a main form by a Quick view component bound to a lookup columnHidden when the lookup is empty. No form scripts, no header, footer or navigation, no custom controls, one single-column tab. Can't be activated or deactivated.No
CardCompact layout used in views, suited to small screens such as mobile devicesOrdered with the form order like the other sets.No

Logic and components on a form

RequirementUse
Show or hide, lock, require, set a value or default, show an error or recommendation; no code; main or quick create formBusiness rule (§3.3). Scope: one form, All Forms, or Entity (the table and all its forms). Model-driven-only actions such as Lock, Set Visibility, Set Business Required and Recommendation are ignored when a rule runs server-side. Multiselect choice columns aren't supported.
Logic a rule can't express (multiselect choice, asynchronous calls, cross-table logic)JavaScript form script: add the web resource under Form libraries, then register a handler for OnLoad, OnSave, OnChange, TabStateChange or OnReadyStateComplete. Use getFormContext; Xrm.Page is deprecated.
One related row, read-onlyQuick view component: Components > Quick view > choose the lookup column, related table and quick view form.
A list of related rowsSubgrid; add the Power Apps grid control from Components > Grid when users need inline editing.
A record-aware visual built from a promptGenerative page component: Components > Display > Generative page.

Copilot and AI features on forms

  • Column suggestions: select Get AI generated column suggestions in the New form dialog; Copilot proposes columns from the form name and description for quick view and quick create forms, and the maker reviews them. The docs describe it with preview wording.
  • Form fill assistance (Smart paste and file upload): main and quick create forms only; needs the modern look, the Allow form fill assistance column property and a Power Apps premium or Dynamics 365 Enterprise or Premium licence. The Power Apps article calls it a "production ready preview"; Smart paste is labelled preview.
  • Row summary: an AI summary in the Insights bar at the top of main forms (and an inline Summary action in views); the table must be configured to display summaries (§1.2). Also on forms: the Agent Response component (Components > Artificial Intelligence; Preview).
Exam traps
  • Quick create, quick view and card forms can't be assigned to security roles; the form at the top of the form order is the one everybody uses.
  • A quick create form can't hold subgrids, quick view forms, web resources, iFrames, notes or Bing Maps, and its single section always has three columns.
  • Quick view forms are read-only, run no scripts and show nothing when the lookup is empty.
  • Form fill assistance works on main and quick create forms only, and each target column needs Allow form fill assistance.

Create and configure views for model-driven apps

A view defines the columns a table's list shows, their order and width, the default sort and the default filters. Charts and dashboard lists also read data through views. Views belong to the table, so every view is available to every app that includes the table until you restrict the app.

View typeOwnerFacts to remember
PersonalOne user; others see it only if it is sharedCreated with Create view on the app command bar; needs at least User-level access to the Saved View table. Listed above the system and public views.
SystemThe organizationQuick Find, Advanced Find, Associated, Lookup. Not in the view selector, not usable in subgrids or dashboard lists, can't be deleted or deactivated.
PublicThe organizationGeneral-purpose views in the view selector; usable in subgrids and dashboard lists. A view you create in the maker portal is a public view.

Build and expose a public view

  1. Solutions > your solution > the table > Views > New view; enter a name and select Create.
  2. In the view designer add columns (+ View column or drag from the Table columns pane), then set filters (Filter by in a column header, or Edit filters) and sorting (Sort by, Then sort by).
  3. Select Save and publish.
  4. In the app designer open Pages, select the table's view page and check the Views tab: the view must be in the app. Save, then Publish.
  • Filter expressions: Edit filters > Add > Add row, Add group or Add related table. A group combines rows with And by default and can switch to Or. A condition on a related table supports only Contains data.
  • Default view: only a public view can be the table's default: "..." beside the view > Set as default view. A public view that is the default can't be turned off. Users see the maker's default unless they have pinned a different view as their personal default.
  • Editable grids: the Power Apps grid control supports inline editing, grouping and aggregation, but Enable editing defaults to No. Add it to all views of a table on the table's Controls tab in classic solution explorer, or to one subgrid in the form designer (Components > Grid > Power Apps grid control). The legacy Editable grid and the older read-only grids are Deprecated.
  • Natural-language grid search: a search box on the grid that filters, sorts and searches text but can't aggregate, group or add columns. A string of two words or fewer runs a text search; use more than two words for a natural-language query, or put a longer phrase in quotes to force a text search. An admin controls it under Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Data exploration. It needs a Power Apps premium or Dynamics 365 Enterprise or Premium licence.
Exam traps
  • System views never appear in the view selector and can't be deleted or deactivated; only public views can be turned off.
  • The related-table condition in a view filter allows only Contains data.
  • Adding the Power Apps grid control doesn't make a grid editable: Enable editing must be set to Yes.
  • By default all views are available in an app; removing one in the app designer doesn't delete it from the environment.

Create generative pages by using natural language

A generative page is a page in a model-driven app that an AI agent builds from your prompt: it writes React (TypeScript) code for the UI and the logic, renders it, and lets you refine it by chat or in code. Canvas apps don't support generative pages, and users see a page only after the app is published.

GA core feature (release plan: global GA 2 Apr 2026). Preview Power Platform connectors, Dataverse custom APIs, the Include images tool and Application Insights telemetry. A few older articles still label the whole feature preview.

Create a page in the browser

  1. Open the model-driven app for editing (Apps > Edit).
  2. In the app designer select Add page > Generative page, then Describe a page. The same dialog also lists existing generative pages to add (filter: Published by default).
  3. Write the prompt (functional requirements, optional UX details, at most 50,000 characters) and attach data: Add data > Add table (up to six Dataverse tables). Attach image adds a sketch or mockup.
  4. Select Generate page. The agent streams its thinking, writes code, transpiles it and renders the result (Preview tab).
  5. Iterate: chat with the agent, edit on the Code tab (Edit, then Save or Cancel), use Compare from the second iteration, attach a screenshot, or run the Accessibility assistant and Auto fix.
  6. Save, then Save and Publish, which publishes all pending app changes including the generative pages.
Data sourceHow to add itStatus
Dataverse tablesAdd data > Add table; up to six tables per pageGA
Power Platform connectorsAdd data > Connectors; needs a connection and a connection reference created in the Default SolutionPreview
Dataverse custom APIAdd > Custom API; global and table-bound actions and functions; EntityCollection binding and Entity parameters unsupported; runs as the signed-in userPreview
Stock imagesInclude images tool; 25,000 curated images, not AI-generatedPreview
  • Where it runs: in-browser authoring is available for environments in the United States, Great Britain, Australia and Singapore, prompts must be US English, and GPT-4.1 is the only model offered. AI code generation tools (for example GitHub Copilot CLI) are the route the docs recommend: newer models, available worldwide on public clouds, several pages and tables in one run. The maker experience needs no extra AI or message credits.
  • Limits: no collaboration (one maker per page at a time), only a fixed list of column data types, and generated code isn't guaranteed production-ready, so the maker validates it.
  • Inputs: recordId, entityName and data; ask for them in the prompt (for example "accept an account recordId").
  • Embed in a form: publish a page that accepts recordId, then form designer > Components > Display > Generative page; the form passes the current record ID automatically.
  • Inside the page data calls go through dataApi: createRow, deleteRow, getChoices, queryTable, retrieveRow, setPageOutput, updateRow.
  • Solutions: pages are solution-aware through the app. Solutions > Add existing > App > Model-driven app, then export managed or unmanaged with the sitemap included; pages appear as UX Agent Project rows. After import only the first prompt and the last published code arrive, not the chat history.

Open a generative page from script (find the page ID in the app designer: select the page and copy the GUID in the Generative page field of the properties pane):

var pageInput = {
    pageType: "generative",
    pageId: "<genPageID>",
    entityName: "account",
    recordId: "00aa00aa-bb11-cc22-dd33-44ee44ee44ee"
};
var navigationOptions = {
    target: 2,          // 1 = inline, 2 = dialog
    position: 1,        // 1 = centered, 2 = side
    width: { value: 70, unit: "%" },
    height: { value: 80, unit: "%" },
    title: "Account insights"
};
Xrm.Navigation.navigateTo(pageInput, navigationOptions);
Generative pageCustom pageEmbedded canvas app
Authored withNatural-language prompts; React and TypeScriptPower Apps Studio, Power FxPower Apps Studio
Where it appearsNavigation page, form component, dialog, side paneNavigation page, dialog, side paneModel-driven form only
navigateTopageType: "generative" + pageIdpageType: "custom" + nameNot applicable
DataDataverse; connectors and custom APIs in previewDataverse and all Power Apps connectorsCanvas data sources
ConstraintsSix tables; one maker at a timeKeep to 25 per app; one maker per pageA limit on the number per form
Exam traps
  • The route is Add page > Generative page > Describe a page. An older article still shows Pages tab > New > Describe a page.
  • Connectors, custom APIs and Include images are preview; only Dataverse tables are the GA data source, and the limit is six tables.
  • Generative pages exist only in model-driven apps, and nothing is visible to users until you Save and Publish.
  • A generative page uses pageType: "generative" with pageId; name belongs to custom pages.
  • Only the first prompt and the last published code travel with the solution.

Compose a model-driven app

Create the app inside a solution so it can be moved: Solutions > your solution > New > App > Model-driven app > name > Create, then Add page, Save, Publish and Play. Model-driven apps need Dataverse. Use the modern app designer: its command bar has Back, Add page, Settings, Edit form, Comments, Save, Publish and Play, and the left panes are Pages (Navigation with areas, groups and subareas, plus All other pages), Data and Automation (business process flows). The classic app designer is Deprecated (the maker article says that since October 2023 the Switch to classic command is no longer available by default, but the admin settings article lists Show the Switch to classic buttons in Power Apps with a default of On, so check the environment's setting before relying on the classic designers); the Validate command exists only in the classic designer because the modern designer validates while you build.

Add page typeUse it for
Dataverse tableA list (view) page for a table; it also adds the associated form page
DashboardSystem, interactive or Power BI embedded dashboards
Generative pageA page built from a natural-language prompt
Custom pageA canvas-based page with Power Fx; keep to 25 or fewer per app
Web resourceAn HTML, JavaScript, CSS or image file
Navigation linkA URL that opens in a new browser tab
  • Navigation: ellipsis beside Navigation > Settings (or Settings > Navigation). Show Home, Show Recent and Show Pinned are on by default; Enable collapsible groups and Enable Areas are off. Enable Areas is on for apps that already have several areas and can't be turned off while they do.
  • Group: Pages > ellipsis beside Navigation > New group. Area: turn on Enable Areas, then the area switcher under Pages > New area. Clear Show in navigation to keep a page out of the sitemap; Remove from navigation removes a group, page or area.
  • Settings dialog tabs: General (name, description, icon), Advanced settings (unique name, welcome page, primary mobile player), Features, Navigation, Upcoming (preview features). A settings change takes effect only after Publish. Create description using AI needs a managed environment.
  • Coauthoring: several makers can edit at once, but there is no autosave: select Save, because unsaved changes are removed after eight hours. It isn't available in Germany, China and Government Cloud; changes in the form and view designers don't sync live.
  • Distribute: add the app to a solution (Add existing > App > Model-driven app), export, import, then assign security roles in the target environment.
Exam traps
  • The area switcher is missing until Enable Areas is turned on; Enable collapsible groups only lets users expand and collapse subareas.
  • Save keeps your work; Publish makes it visible to users, including Settings changes.
  • A table page adds a view page and a form page, so removing "the page" from navigation doesn't remove the table's forms and views.
  • The Validate button belongs to the deprecated classic designer.

Configure access to forms and views for model-driven apps

Access to forms and views is decided at two levels: app level (which forms, views and charts an app exposes) and role level (which main form or public view a user gets). Neither one secures data: rows are still filtered by the privileges in the user's roles (§1.2).

GoalWhere and how
Show only some forms in one appApp designer > Pages > the table's form page > right pane: In this app / Not in this app > ellipsis > Remove or Add > Publish. All forms are included by default.
Show only some views or charts in one appPages > the table's view page > Views or Charts tab > Remove or Add > Save > Publish.
A different main form per roleSolutions > table > Forms > select the main form > Form settings > Security role > Everyone or Specific security roles > Save and Publish. Main forms only.
Which form is the defaultForm settings > Form order: choose the Main, Quick Create, Quick View or Card set and drag. Order sets priority, not permission.
A form for users whose roles have none assignedForm settings > Fallback forms (tick the forms). Main forms only.
Block a main form for everyoneSet the main form Inactive.
A different public view per roleSet EnableRoleBasedSystemViews to true (OrganizationSettingsEditor, System Administrator), then Solutions > table > Views > select a non-default public view > View settings > Specific security roles > Save and Publish.
  • Form settings has four areas: Security role, Form order, Fallback forms and Form access checker.
  • Fallback strategies: a contingency form (assign it only to System Administrator) or a generic form (the least specialised form is the fallback, ranked last in the form order). A user's chosen form stays their default.
  • Role-based views: only public views, and never the default public view. The roles listed come from the root business unit. Only the table's list view selector is filtered; subgrids and associated grids keep their selectors, and Manage and share views still lists everything. Assignment is effective after Save and publish; changing back to Everyone can take up to 24 hours. Move it to production with a solution that holds the tables and views.
  • The Views overview article links to this feature as "(preview)"; the article itself shows no preview banner.
Exam traps
  • Form order isn't access control, and fallback forms and role assignment apply to main forms only.
  • Setting a main form to Inactive removes it for every user, including the roles you wanted to serve.
  • A default public view can't be assigned security roles, and the setting filters only the table list view selector.
  • Having access to a view or form doesn't grant access to its data.

Configure access to model-driven apps

Model-driven apps are shared by assigning security roles to the app (or by sharing with users or teams); unlike canvas apps, no email with a link is sent. Sequence: make sure a role has the table privileges the app needs, assign that role to the app, then give users the link. Apps > ellipsis beside the app > Share > choose security roles (or People) > Share. To get the link, go to Apps > select the app > Details and copy the Web link (or the Mobile QR code).

User holdsWhat they see
Basic User only (read on the Model-driven App table)Only apps that have a role of theirs assigned to the app
Create and write on the Model-driven App table: System Administrator, System Customizer, Environment MakerAll apps in the environment (maker persona); they can edit them
Environment Maker aloneApps, but no access to core or custom tables to work with data
  • Prerequisites: the sharer has admin privileges and a role with equal or greater privileges than the roles being assigned (typically System Administrator or System Customizer); the user exists in the environment (a Microsoft 365 account isn't enough); the user has the right licence. Premium components such as maps or address input need Power Apps licences.
  • Custom tables: an administrator must configure privileges on the custom tables in a security role, otherwise users can't work with the rows.
  • Large audiences: use a group team backed by a Microsoft Entra Security or Microsoft 365 group, give the team a role, and share the app with that role.
  • Hide an app: Solutions > the solution > select the app > ellipsis > Turn off. It leaves Power Apps Mobile and Office app lists and can't be played or shared from make.powerapps.com, but direct links still work. Managed apps can't be turned off.
  • App access checker: https://<environmentURL>/WebResources/msdyn_AppAccessChecker.html, search by UPN or email. Visible, License and Security must all be Yes.
  • The Managed Environments Limit sharing setting covers canvas apps, solution-aware cloud flows and agents; it doesn't list model-driven apps.
Exam traps
  • Sharing a model-driven app sends no email; the maker passes on the link.
  • App access (a role assigned to the app, plus a licence) is separate from data access (table privileges in the role); empty grids point to missing table privileges.
  • Turning an app off doesn't secure it: direct links keep working.
  • Environment Maker can open every app but has no table access by itself.

Create and configure model-driven app charts and dashboards

System (organization-owned)Personal (user-owned)
ChartSavedQueryVisualization; called a system chart; can't be assigned or shared; solution-aware; must be publishedUserQueryVisualization; listed under My Charts; can be assigned and shared
DashboardCreated by an admin or customizer; visible to all app users once publishedMy Dashboards; the creator can share it (if the role allows) and set it as their default

Build and publish a system chart

  1. Solutions > the solution > the table > Charts (under Data experiences) > New chart.
  2. In the designer pick the Column (value axis), the Aggregate and the Chart type, then Next.
  3. Pick the category column (horizontal axis) and Apply.
  4. Save, then Publish. If the app lists specific charts, also add the chart on the app designer's Charts tab.
  • Aggregates: numeric columns offer Count: All, Count: Non-empty, Average, Max, Min and Sum; non-numeric columns only the two counts. NULLs are ignored in min, max and average; zeros count.
  • Options: Add a series; Stacked and 100% Stacked only for bar, column and area charts; Top/Bottom via Set minimum and maximum values; a comparison chart has up to two categories and one series; Export chart and Import chart (XML); Switch to Classic. Charts show views returning up to 50,000 records. The article that describes this designer is labelled Preview.
  • Chart on a form: select a subgrid and choose Show chart only.

Dashboards

  • Standard dashboard: Solutions > New > Dashboard > layout (2-column, 3-column, 3-column varied width, 4-column, or Power BI embedded) > select a component icon > Add Component (Record Type, View, Chart) > Save, Close, Publish. The designer allows up to six components (six is the default maximum; 20 is only the ceiling that an on-premises administrator can set).
  • Interactive experience dashboard: system dashboards that an administrator or customizer builds in a solution, in the classic interface (Switch to classic; whether that button is visible depends on the environment's Show the Switch to classic buttons in Power Apps setting, which Microsoft's articles describe inconsistently). Multi-stream shows several data streams (each stream on one table); single-stream shows one stream plus tiles. The charts act as visual filters. Enable security roles limits who sees it. Queues aren't solution-aware.
  • Power BI embedded: Solutions > New > Dashboard > Power BI embedded (choose report or dashboard; Use environment variable to move it between environments). In an app: Add page > Dashboard > System dashboards picker > Power BI dashboards. Users need Power BI licences and authorization.
  • Sharing a personal dashboard doesn't share its personal charts and views; the owner shares each separately.
  • Visualize: the AI chart pane on a grid (Pie, Donut, Bar, Column, Clustered Bar, Stacked Bar, Clustered Column, Stacked Column, Line, Histogram, Bubble). Save As makes a personal chart. Needs a Power Apps premium or Dynamics 365 Enterprise or Premium licence.
NeedUse
Governed organization-wide visual that travels in a solutionSystem chart
Unrelated KPIs on one pageStandard dashboard (up to six components)
Triage workload with real-time streams and row actionsInteractive experience dashboard (admin, classic)
Analytics from other sourcesPower BI embedded dashboard
Quick ad-hoc chart on a viewVisualize, then Save As (personal chart)
Exam traps
  • System charts can't be assigned or shared; only personal charts can.
  • Only an administrator can create an interactive experience dashboard, and the designer is the classic one.
  • A chart on a view with more than 50,000 records fails with "The maximum record limit is exceeded".
  • Sharing a personal dashboard doesn't share the personal charts and views inside it.
  • Stacking works only on bar, column and area charts.

sections.title: 2.2 Create canvas apps
sections.html:
Skills measured: create a canvas app using data • design apps for accessibility, performance, responsiveness and usability • automate business processes from canvas apps • named formulas, user-defined functions and component libraries • manage variables and collections • implement error handling • test canvas apps, including Monitor • create a Copilot Studio agent from a canvas app. Build one Dataverse-backed app and push it through every topic: add a flow, a component library, App.Formulas entries, an IfError save button, a Live monitor session and an agent made from the app.

Create a canvas app using data

PathWhere to clickWhat you get / requirement
Existing Dataverse tableHome > Start with data > Dataverse > pick a table > Create appA single-page responsive gallery app bound to the table. The maker needs the Environment Maker role; custom security roles aren't supported for canvas maker scenarios.
New tablesStart with data > Create new dataThe Create new tables designer: table designer or the Copilot panel (natural-language prompt); Save and exit generates the app. Copilot needs Dataverse and the system customizer role.
SharePoint listStart with data > SharePoint > site URL > Connect > list > Create app (or Integrate > Power Apps > Create an app inside the list)New apps are a single responsive screen; older generated apps have three (Browse, Details, Edit).
ExcelStart with data > Upload file, or an Excel Online (Business) connectionThe data must be an Excel table. Upload file converts it into a Dataverse table (first 20 rows appear immediately, 5 GB maximum); Excel Online (Business) leaves the workbook in the cloud as the source.
PlanStart with a plan > Create a planPlan designer proposes roles, tables, apps, flows and agents from a description. GA Needs Dataverse (see §1.1).
BlankCreate > Create from blankPick Responsive, Tablet size or Phone size and connect the data yourself for full control of layout.
  • Copilot admin controls: the Copilot overview states that some Copilot features in Power Apps are in preview. Generally available Copilot features are on by default and only Microsoft Support can turn them off; preview Copilot features can be turned off per environment (admin center Settings > Features > Copilot) or for the tenant (Copilot in Power Apps (preview)). The tenant switch affects makers only, not the Copilot control in apps.

Delegation and the data row limit

  • Delegation means the data source runs the query. If any part of a formula is nondelegable, none of it is delegated: the app downloads only the first 500 records (the Data row limit) and evaluates the rest locally, which gives wrong answers on bigger tables. Parts that evaluate to the same constant for every record (control values and variables) don't block delegation. For date functions such as Today() and Now() Microsoft's articles disagree: the general delegation article treats them as constants, while the Dataverse connector's delegation table lists them as not delegable, so check the connector's table and avoid relying on them in a filter over a large table.
  • Change the limit under Settings > General > Data row limit: range 1–10,000, default 500. Set it to 1 while testing so every nondelegable formula fails visibly. Raising the limit hides the problem and slows the app.
  • A nondelegable formula over a delegable source (Dataverse, SharePoint, SQL Server, Salesforce) gets a yellow triangle and a blue wavy underline. In-memory data — collections, context-variable tables, imported static Excel data — never delegates and never warns.
Delegable (if the source supports it)Not delegable
Filter, Search, First, LookUp, Sort/SortByColumns (a single column name only), Sum, Average, Min, Max, CountRows, Count; And, Or, Not, =, <>, <, >, In (base-table columns), StartsWith, EndsWith, IsBlankFirstN, Last, LastN, Collect, ClearCollect, Concat, GroupBy, Ungroup, Choices, If, *, /, Mod, Text()/Value() casts of a column, and Len over a column
  • Dataverse: Search and StartsWith work on Text columns only; Len and TrimEnds aren't delegable; aggregate functions are limited to 50,000 rows; CountRows returns a cached value, so use CountIf(table, True) for an exact count under 50,000.
  • SharePoint: Not doesn't delegate; IsBlank on a Text column doesn't either, but Filter(list, Col = Blank()) does (equals only, not <>). Always check the connector's own delegation table.
  • Reduce risk by filtering on the server, creating a server-side view for heavy joins (a query can expand or join up to 20 tables), and never copying a large table into a collection just to silence a warning.
Exam traps
  • The data row limit tops out at 10,000 (default 500). The signal is a warning (yellow triangle, blue underline), not an error, and only delegable sources show it.
  • ClearCollect(col, BigTable) is itself nondelegable: it copies only the first rows up to the limit, and later filters on the collection never warn.
  • Search matches text anywhere in a column; use StartsWith for “begins with”.
  • Dataverse canvas makers need Environment Maker (custom roles unsupported); Copilot table creation needs system customizer.
  • Removed Edit with Copilot (2026-01-06) and creating an app from an image or Figma design (2025-10-21) no longer exist in the maker experience.

Design apps for accessibility, performance, responsiveness, and usability

Accessibility

  • Accessibility checker: App checker icon (upper right of Studio) > Accessibility. Issues are sorted by severity (Error, Warning, Tip) and then by screen; select an issue to open the property, fix it, then Re-check.
Checker issueSeverityFix
Missing accessible labelErrorPut text in AccessibleLabel of every interactive control (a button, or an image/icon that has OnSelect)
Focus isn't showingErrorSet FocusedBorderThickness above 0 and keep the focus border high-contrast
Missing captions; Turn off autostartWarningFill ClosedCaptionsURL on Audio/Video; set Autostart to false
Revise screen name; Check the order of the screen itemsTipRename default screen names; avoid TabIndex above 0
  • Keyboard and screen readers: TabIndex 0 for interactive controls and -1 for non-interactive ones (AcceptsFocus true/false on modern controls); hidden and disabled controls are skipped. Reading and tab order follow screen position (top to bottom, then left to right), not Tree-view order, so group related controls in a Container. Positive TabIndex values are discouraged: the checker raises a Tip and one accessibility page says values above 0 are treated as 0.
  • Live (Off, Polite, Assertive) and Role (Default, Heading1–4) exist on Label only. An empty AccessibleLabel on an image, icon or shape hides it from screen readers.
  • Contrast: text at least 4.5:1; large text and non-text elements (icons, borders, focus border) at least 3:1.

Performance

The official guidance rests on four principles: optimize page loads, small data payloads, optimized query patterns and fast calculations.

SymptomUse
Many values calculated in OnStartNamed formulas in App.Formulas: calculated just in time, in parallel and only when needed
Navigate in OnStart picks the first screenApp.StartScreen (Navigate in OnStart is retired). It can't use behavior functions, global variables or collections; keep the first screen blank or light
Several independent data loads at startConcurrent(f1, f2, ...): two or more behavior formulas that don't depend on each other
Large tables copied into collectionsDon't. Collections suit small data with many calculations (an order basket); read other data natively with delegable Filter
Wide tablesExplicit column selection (on by default); add ShowColumns when column lineage is lost
Flows used to fill collectionsAvoid: every flow start costs about 0.6 seconds
App.Formulas:    CurrentUser = LookUp(Users, 'Primary Email' = User().Email);
App.StartScreen: If(Param("AdminMode") = "1", AdminScreen, HomeScreen)
App.OnStart:     Concurrent(ClearCollect(colCategories, Categories), ClearCollect(colRegions, Regions))

Responsiveness

  • Settings > Display: Scale to fit (default On) scales screens to the window. Turning it Off activates responsiveness, switches Lock aspect ratio off automatically and makes each screen's Width and Height track the window instead of the design size. Lock orientation remains your choice: it only decides whether the app supports device rotation (the Building responsive canvas apps walkthrough switches off Scale to fit, Lock aspect ratio and Lock orientation together).
  • Lay out with Horizontal/Vertical containers (flexible width and height, fill portions, align, justify, gap, wrap) or with Parent.Width/Parent.Height formulas; inside gallery templates use Parent.TemplateWidth/TemplateHeight. Data table, Charts and Add picture aren't supported inside layout containers.
  • Parent.Size returns ScreenSize.Small (1), Medium (2), Large (3) or ExtraLarge (4), calculated from App.SizeBreakpoints: default [600, 900, 1200], phone apps [1200, 1800, 2400]. Example: Visible = Parent.Size >= ScreenSize.Medium.
  • The authoring canvas does not react to sizing formulas; save, publish and test on real window sizes.

Usability

  • Follow the design guidelines: one form for new, edit and view; gallery and forms on separate screens; containers instead of groups; no nested galleries; meaningful names (prefixes such as btn, gal, txt; gbl, loc, col for global, context and collection variables).
  • Modern controls and themes (Fluent) are turned on under Settings > Updates > New.
Exam traps
  • A missing AccessibleLabel is an Error, not a warning. A wrong reading order is fixed with position and containers, not by giving controls TabIndex values above 0.
  • Responsive needs Scale to fit Off. Lock orientation and the orientation or aspect-ratio pickers don't make an app responsive.
  • Navigate in OnStart is retired; App.StartScreen replaces it but can't read global variables or collections.
  • Concurrent needs at least two independent formulas and speeds up loading only; it does nothing for delegation.
  • Raising the data row limit is never the performance fix.

Automate business processes from canvas apps

  1. In Studio select Power Automate on the authoring menu (the pane is on by default) > Create new flow (a template such as Click a button in Power Apps to send an email, or Create from blank) or Add a flow (Add a flow from this environment).
  2. The flow must start with a Power Apps trigger, and you need access to it and to the flows of the same solution. Added flows are listed under In your app.
  3. Call it from a behavior property with FlowName.Run(arg1, arg2); an existing formula on the property is preserved. Save and publish.
PowerAppsbutton.Run()
SendReview.Run(txtApprover.Text, Gallery1.Selected.ID)
IfError(SendReview.Run(txtApprover.Text, Gallery1.Selected.ID),
        Notify("Flow failed: " & FirstError.Message, NotificationType.Error))
  • Maintenance (ellipsis next to the flow): Edit (save before closing), Refresh, Remove from app (the flow stays in the environment). After a flow is changed in Power Automate you must Refresh it in Studio, or it can fail even in apps that were already published. The classic pane is meant for troubleshooting only and will be retired soon; to use it, turn on Enable Classic Power Automate pane under Settings > Upcoming features > Retired tab.
  • Security: arguments sent to a flow are visible as network traffic and can be changed by an outside actor. Validate them inside the flow, for example by checking the e-mail domain before sending.
  • Return data: end the flow with Respond to a Power App or flow (the limits article writes “PowerApp”). Inbound requests have a 120-second limit; actions placed after the response keep running, so respond as soon as the value exists and let long work continue.
RequirementUse
Quick transactional read or write on DataversePower Fx (Patch, LookUp) or a Dataverse action called directly from Power Fx: faster and simpler than a flow
E-mail, approvals, multi-system orchestration, long-running or asynchronous work, run historyA flow with a Power Apps trigger (building flows: §3.1)
Result needed in the app right awayRespond to a Power App or flow, finishing within 120 seconds
Exam traps
  • Only flows with a Power Apps trigger can be added to an app; an automated or scheduled flow can't.
  • Flow arguments aren't secret and the app can't prove who changed them: validate in the flow.
  • Editing the flow in Power Automate doesn't update the app by itself — use Refresh in the Power Automate pane.
  • A response must come back inside 120 seconds; put Respond before the long-running steps, not after.
  • Run() returns data only when the flow has a response action, and every flow start adds latency (about 0.6 s).

Create reuseable components, including named formulas, user-defined functions, and component libraries

NeedUse
A value or derived value used in many places (colors, current user)Named formula
A parameterised calculationUser-defined function (UDF)
A reusable action with side effects (Set, Notify, Collect, Patch)Behavior UDF: body in { }, return type Void
Reusable UI with its own properties and eventsCanvas component
The same component in many apps with controlled updatesComponent library
A value that changes as the user worksA variable (Set, UpdateContext), not a named formula
// App object > Formulas property; each definition ends with a semicolon
BGColor = ColorValue(Param("BackgroundColor"));
UserInfo = LookUp(Users, 'Primary Email' = User().Email);
LineTotal(Qty: Number, Price: Number, Discount: Number): Number = Qty * Price * (1 - Discount);
Spend(Amount: Number): Void = {
    If(Amount > Savings,
        Error($"{Amount} is more than available savings"),
        Set(Savings, Savings - Amount);
        Set(Spent, Spent + Amount)
    );
};
Book := Type({Title: Text, Author: Text});
  • Named formulas are immutable, always available (no OnStart timing dependency), always up to date, can refer to each other in any order and are calculated only when needed. They can't use behavior functions and can't be circular (a = b; with b = a;).
  • UDFs: every parameter and the return value must be typed (built-in types, data-source names or Type() types); recursion isn't supported; the fields of a record argument must be a subset of the type's fields, so extra fields cause an error. User-defined types use := with Type(). UDFs, UDTs and enhanced component properties are GA according to Microsoft's announcements.
  • Components: Tree view > Components > New component; a New custom property is Input or Output. Enhanced component properties add the types Data, Function, Action and Event. Access app scope On exposes global variables, collections, controls and tabular data sources; components in a library never get app scope.
  1. Create: Component libraries (left navigation, or More > Discover all > App enhancements) > New component library, then build the components.
  2. Save (optionally Save with version notes), then Publish: only published versions reach apps.
  3. Consume: in an app choose Insert > Get more components and pick the components; they appear under Library components.
  4. Update: a notification appears when the app is edited (Review > Update, version notes shown), or select Check for updates in the Insert components panel.
  • Edit component on a library component offers Create a copy. The copy sits under Custom and never receives library updates; existing instances stay linked. A library that an app uses can't be deleted. Sharing works like apps: a co-owner can use, edit and share but not delete or change the owner. Library screens are for testing only, and libraries don't show in Power Apps Mobile.
  • Libraries are the recommended way to reuse components across apps; Retired importing components from one app into another.
Exam traps
  • Named formulas take no parameters and no side effects. A UDF without parameter types or without a return type is invalid, and recursion isn't allowed.
  • Saving a library isn't enough: consuming apps see only published versions.
  • Editing a library component inside an app makes a local copy that stops receiving updates.
  • A canvas component library is low-code; code components belong to the Power Apps component framework (PCF).
  • Components in a library can't reach app scope, so pass data in through input properties.

Manage variables and collections

KindCreated withScopeTypical use
Global variableSet(name, value)Whole appFlags and counters changed from any screen; holds any value, including records and tables
Context variableUpdateContext({name: value}) or the third argument of NavigateOne screenScreen flags and parameters passed in on navigation
CollectionCollect, ClearCollectWhole app (a table)Small editable tables, baskets, small caches
Named formulaName = expression; in App.FormulasWhole app, read-onlyStatic or derived values that must stay current
Set(gblUser, Office365Users.MyProfile())
UpdateContext({locShowPanel: true})
Navigate(DetailScreen, ScreenTransition.Fade, {locItem: Gallery1.Selected})
ClearCollect(colBasket, Filter(Products, Active = true))
Collect(colBasket, {Product: Gallery1.Selected.Name, Qty: 1})
Remove(colBasket, Gallery2.Selected)
Patch(Orders, Defaults(Orders), {Title: txtTitle.Text})
Clear(colBasket)
  • Variables are declared implicitly by the function that sets them, hold blank until set, must keep one type and live in memory: values are lost when the app closes. Persist them with Patch to a data source or, for small data, with SaveData/LoadData (limited to 1 MB in a browser or Teams).
  • Navigate(Screen [, Transition [, UpdateContextRecord]]): the optional record sets context variables on the target screen and is the only way to set a context variable from outside its screen. The default transition is ScreenTransition.None.
  • If a context variable and a global or collection share a name, the context variable wins; write [@Name] to reach the global. A global variable can't share a name with a collection or a control.
  • Collect adds a value, record or table rows and creates the collection if needed; ClearCollect = Clear + Collect; Clear works only on collections (RemoveIf(DataSource, true) deletes rows in a data source). Remove(DataSource, Record [, RemoveFlags.All]) and RemoveIf(DataSource, Condition) delete; Patch(DataSource, Defaults(DataSource), {...}) creates a row.
  • Prefer a named formula for static or derived values, With for a value used in one formula, and variables only for state that changes. Collections sit in device memory: keep them small (ShowColumns, Filter) and use ClearCollect rather than Clear followed by Collect.
Exam traps
  • UpdateContext takes a record and sets variables on the screen where the formula runs, not on the screen you navigate to.
  • Collect on every refresh duplicates rows (use ClearCollect); Clear(Accounts) on a data source isn't valid.
  • Collections, With, Set and UpdateContext data live in memory: no delegation and no delegation warning.
  • Variables vanish when the app closes; SaveData is capped at 1 MB in browsers and Teams.

Implement error handling

Formula-level error management is on by default in new apps. Confirm that Settings > Updates > Retired > Disable formula-level management is Off: when it is on, errors turn into blanks and IfError, IsError and Error don't work correctly. The model has three parts: handle (IfError, IsError, IsBlankOrError), report (App.OnError) and create or rethrow (Error).

IfError(1 / x, 0)                                      // replace the error with a value
IfError(Patch(Orders, Defaults(Orders), {Title: txtTitle.Text}),
        Notify("Order could not be saved", NotificationType.Error),   // runs on error, then stops
        Navigate(ConfirmationScreen))                  // default result: only when nothing failed
If(IsError(Value(txtQty.Text)), Notify("Enter a number", NotificationType.Warning))
If(StartDate > EndDate, Error({Kind: ErrorKind.Validation, Message: "Start Date must be before End Date"}))
IfError(a / b, If(FirstError.Kind <> ErrorKind.Div0, Error(FirstError), -1))   // handle one kind, rethrow the rest
// App.OnError
Trace($"Error {FirstError.Message} in {FirstError.Source}"); Error(FirstError)
  • IfError(Value1, Replacement1 [, Value2, Replacement2, ... [, DefaultResult]]) tests values in order, runs the first matching replacement and stops. With no error it returns DefaultResult (otherwise the last value). The result types must be compatible.
  • Inside replacements, FirstError (= First(AllErrors)) and AllErrors expose Kind, Message, Source, Observed and Details (network errors: HttpStatusCode, HttpResponse).
  • Chained behavior formulas don't stop: in Patch(DS1, ...); Patch(DS2, ...) the second Patch still runs after the first fails. Wrap the steps in IfError to stop.
  • IsBlankOrError(x) = Or(IsBlank(x), IsError(x)). Use it instead of IsBlank in migrated apps, because blank used to stand for both null and error.
  • App.OnError runs for every unhandled error with FirstError/AllErrors. It can log or suppress the banner but can't replace the error; Error(FirstError) rethrows it so the default banner still shows.
  • Data sources and forms: a failed Patch, Collect, Remove or SubmitForm fills Errors(DataSource [, Record]) (columns Record, Column, Message, Error). Forms use OnSuccess/OnFailure and the form's Error/ErrorKind properties.
  • Notify(Message [, NotificationType [, Timeout]]): types Error, Information (default), Success, Warning; default timeout 10 seconds (the argument is in milliseconds, 0 keeps the banner until dismissed); 500-character message limit; formerly named ShowError. Trace(Message [, TraceSeverity [, CustomRecord [, TraceOptions]]]) writes to Live monitor and Application Insights; severities Information (default), Warning, Error, Critical.
GoalUse
Replace a bad value, or stop a chain after a failed stepIfError
Branch on an error without replacing itIf(IsError(...), ...)
One place to log or suppress unhandled errorsApp.OnError (with Trace)
Raise a business-rule failureError({Kind: ..., Message: ...})
Tell the user / diagnose in MonitorNotify / Trace
Exam traps
  • App.OnError is not a replacement mechanism; only IfError substitutes a value or stops a chain.
  • A ; chain keeps running after an error; the second action is not skipped.
  • The switch for formula-level error management sits on the Retired tab and is worded as disable.
  • Notify timeout is in milliseconds, and the type argument defaults to Information.
  • Errors surface only when a value is used, and IfError arguments need compatible types (IfError(1/x, "text") fails; wrap with Text()).

Test canvas apps, including using Monitor

SituationTool
Trace events while authoring, or reproduce a problem in the published appLive monitor
Trend of load time and failures over days (time to interactive, data request success rate)Monitor page (Apps > Monitor); recommendations need Managed Environments
Formula problems, unused variablesApp checker
Screen-reader, keyboard and contrast issuesAccessibility checker
Repeatable low-code regression testsTest Studio
Code-first cross-browser automationPower Platform Playwright samples; Power Apps Test Engine is deprecated (April 2026)
  1. Studio session: left pane > Advanced tools > Open live monitor (opens a new tab marked as a Studio session), then play the app.
  2. Published app: Apps > select the app > drop-down next to Details > Live monitor > Play published app.
  3. To see source formulas for the published app, turn on Debug published app (File > Settings) and publish. It degrades performance for all users, so turn it off afterwards. Live monitor itself has no impact on the app.
  • Live monitor needs Environment Admin or Environment Maker. Share a session with Invite (per-user link that expires after 60 minutes) or watch a user with Connect user (app published with Power Apps 3.20042 or later). Trace files download as .json or .csv; only .json can be uploaded again. It isn't supported for Teams-embedded apps, SharePoint custom forms or canvas apps embedded in model-driven apps. Copy monitor link (Power Apps mobile) is Preview.
  • Trace(...) adds your own events. In the grid look for repeated calls, large responses, slow requests and HTTP 429 throttling (for example CountRows evaluated for every added record against Dataverse).
  • Test Studio: Advanced tools > Open tests; you must be the app's creator or a co-owner. Tests are written in Power Fx or recorded and are stored in the app package.
  • A test case is a series of steps; a test suite groups cases that run sequentially with the app state persisted, because the app is not reloaded between cases. An assertion must evaluate to true, for example Assert(kudosAfterTest = kudosBeforeTest + 1, "Kudos count incorrect"). Other step actions: SetProperty, Select, Trace.
  • Record plays the published app and overwrites the steps of an existing case; Publish before Play, otherwise the last published tests run. Suite events: OnTestCaseStart (for example navigate to the first screen), OnTestCaseComplete, OnTestSuiteComplete. Not supported: components, PCF code components, nested galleries, media controls.
Exam traps
  • Two things are called Monitor: Live monitor (event stream) and the Monitor page (performance insights).
  • Debug published app slows the app for every user; leaving it on is a mistake.
  • Test Studio records and plays the published version, and suites don't reload the app, so case 2 starts where case 1 ended.
  • Test Engine is deprecated: for new automation the answers are Test Studio (low-code) or Playwright.
  • Trace output from a Test Studio run goes to the test results, not to Live monitor.

Create a Copilot Studio agent from a canvas app

The feature is agent builder in Power Apps (article: Automate your business processes with agent builder in a canvas app). It reads the app's metadata and the goal you describe, generates step-by-step instructions, extracts knowledge and triggers, and combines them with actions (skills) taken from the app. You then edit, test and publish the agent in Microsoft Copilot Studio. The how-to page carries no Preview label.

  1. Sign in to Power Apps, select Agents in the left navigation (under More if hidden) > Create an agent from an app. Alternative: Apps > select the app > Create agent from app.
  2. Select the app > Next.
  3. Pick a suggestion or describe the process to automate in simple, specific language > Next.
  4. Review and edit the generated instructions, then the extracted knowledge and triggers (Regenerate instructions if the goal changes).
  5. Select Create, then finish, test and publish in Copilot Studio.
PrerequisiteDetail
Tenant settingThe tenant admin turns on Publish Copilots with AI features in the Power Platform admin center
DataverseThe environment includes a Dataverse database
CustomizationsBlock unmanaged customizations is disabled
Copilot Studio solutionVersion 2.0.0.649.1 or higher in the environment
  • Limitations: canvas apps only; the deprecated Excel connectors aren't supported (Excel Online (Business) and Excel Online are); if a data-source connection isn't found, actions can't be extracted (the agent gets the convertible ones, or none); available only in regions where Copilot Studio generative agents are.
  • Intended use: automating processes with a focus on data entry; not for medical, legal or hiring purposes. For autonomous operation each action needs maker authentication, and triggers use the maker's credentials.
  • Write instructions in short sentences and a logical order; move a new step into sequence instead of appending it at the end.
FeatureWhat it isStatus
Create an agent from an appGenerates a Copilot Studio agent that automates a process of an existing canvas appListed without a Preview label
Copilot controlChat control inside a canvas app (Dataverse tables)Preview can't be added to new apps from 2026-02-02
Custom Copilot in a canvas appEmbeds a published Copilot Studio agent in the appPreview discontinued for new apps from 2026-02-02
Microsoft Copilot in canvas appsRead-only chat over Dataverse or SharePoint data for app users; needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licensePreview
PlansPlan designer scaffolds a whole solution that can include an agent (§1.1)GA
Exam traps
  • The agent is started in Power Apps (Agents > Create an agent from an app) but finished, tested and published in Copilot Studio.
  • It works only for canvas apps; a model-driven app can't be the source.
  • Block unmanaged customizations must be off, the opposite of a typical production hardening setting.
  • Don't confuse it with the Copilot control, custom Copilot or Microsoft Copilot in canvas apps: those are in-app chat experiences, and the first two are closed to new apps.
  • The tenant switch is still labelled Publish Copilots with AI features although the product term is now “agents”.

sections.title: 3.1 Create cloud flows
sections.html:
Skills measured: Recommend cloud flow triggers • Evaluate and recommend connectors • Manage approvals by using cloud flows • Configure cloud flow actions • Implement flow control with conditions and loops • Test and troubleshoot cloud flows. Build one flow per trigger type, an approval flow per approval type, a List rows flow and a Try/Catch scope, then break each flow on purpose and repair it from the run history.

Recommend cloud flow triggers

GA A cloud flow has exactly one trigger. Choose the flow type, pick the connector trigger, then narrow it so the flow starts only when it must (fewer runs, fewer Power Platform requests).

Flow typeStarts whenExamples
AutomatedAn event occurs in a serviceOutlook When a new email arrives (V3); SharePoint When an item is created or modified; Dataverse When a row is added, modified or deleted
InstantA user selects a button or controlManually trigger a flow; the Power Apps trigger; Dataverse When a row is selected (model-driven app)
ScheduledA time or recurrence is reachedRecurrence: minimum interval 60 seconds, maximum 500 days

Dataverse trigger: When a row is added, modified or deleted

Required: Change type, Table name and Scope; everything else is optional. The author needs user-level Create, Read, Write and Delete privileges on the Callback Registration table, because saving the flow registers a callback with Dataverse. The trigger does not support 1:N or N:N relationships.

SettingWhat it doesDetail to remember
Change typeWhich combination of added, modified and deleted starts the flowWith several selected, triggerOutputs()['body/SdkMessage'] returns Create, Update or Delete
ScopeWhose rows qualify: User, Business Unit, Parent: Child business unit or OrganizationAn organization-owned table allows only Organization
Select columnsComma-separated column names that must be in the updateUpdate only. Fires when the column is in the request, even if its value did not change. Lookup columns are not supported. Leave out the primary key and any column the flow updates itself (infinite loop)
Filter rowsOData expression that must be true after the change is savedExample contoso_amountoverbudget gt 10000. It must not contain $filter=. More efficient than a Condition action
Delay until, Run asDelay until: UTC OData timestamp. Run as: flow owner, row owner (team-owned rows fall back to the flow owner) or modifying userDelay until never expires, unlike the Delay until action. Run as needs the Act on Behalf of Another User privilege and Use invoker's connection on each action

Trigger conditions: filter before the run starts

  1. Select the trigger, open Settings, find Trigger conditions and select Add.
  2. Enter an expression. Every condition must start with @.
  3. Add more conditions if needed. All must be true (AND); for OR write @or(test1, test2, test3).
@greater(triggerOutputs()?['body/contoso_amount'], 100)
  • When a condition is false the flow is not triggered and no run history is logged. A Condition action inside the flow runs after the run has started, so the run still counts. For Outlook, check Folder, Importance or Subject Filter in the trigger, not in a Condition.

Polling or webhook

BehaviourPolling triggerWebhook trigger
How it worksChecks the service at regular intervalsRegisters with the service and is notified of events
Flow turned off, then onPicks up where it left off: pending events are processedProcesses only new events
Avoid the backlogCopy the flow and delete the original (re-registers the trigger)Not needed

Other triggers to recognise

  • When an HTTP request is received: restrict callers with Any user in my tenant (the default for new flows), Specific users in my tenant (emails or service principal object IDs; blank means the whole tenant) or Anyone (legacy, open to anyone with the URL).
  • Power Apps trigger: a flow can be added to a canvas app only if it has this trigger; call it with FlowName.Run(...). The V2 trigger supports embedded and invoker connections but not non-open-API flows. Canvas side: §2.2.
  • Trigger concurrency control: off by default; once applied it cannot be undone without deleting and re-adding the trigger.
RequirementRecommend
Row selected in a model-driven app, or a button in a canvas appDataverse When a row is selected, or the Power Apps trigger
An outside system must start the flowWhen an HTTP request is received, callers limited to the tenant
Events must not be lost while the flow is offA polling trigger (the backlog is processed)
Exam traps
  • Filter rows is OData with no @ and no $filter=. A trigger condition is an expression that starts with @.
  • The Dataverse docs head the Change type box "Trigger condition"; that is not the trigger condition in Settings.
  • Select columns fires when the column is present, not when its value changes; lookup columns never fire it, and the primary key makes every update fire.
  • Polling replays what happened while the flow was off; a webhook does not.

Evaluate and recommend connectors

GA Evaluate a connector with three questions: which license runs it, which data policy group it sits in, and how it is connected in production.

ConnectorClassNotes
SharePoint, Office 365 Outlook, Microsoft Teams, Standard approvalsStandardIncluded in the Free and Microsoft 365 plans
Microsoft DataversePremiumThe only premium connector a data policy cannot block
Custom connectorPremium or trial license to runLimits: 50 per user; 500 requests per minute per connection
LicenseWhat it gives a flow
Free plan or a Microsoft 365 planStandard connectors only
Power Automate Premium (per user)Premium and custom connector entitlements for that user
Process license (per flow)Premium and custom connectors for that flow, whoever runs it; 250,000 actions per day; assigned to a solution-aware flow or a flow group of up to 25 flows
Flow typeLicense contextPremium connector in the flow
Automated or scheduledThe owner, whoever starts it and whatever accounts the connections useOnly the owner needs Premium
Instant (button, app)The invoking user, whatever connections the flow usesEvery user who runs it needs Premium, or the flow gets a Process license
Child flowThe parent's contextUnless the child has its own Process license

Data policies (formerly DLP policies)

GroupMeaningEffect on flows
BusinessConnectors that host business-use dataUsable together only with other Business connectors
Non-BusinessPersonal-use data. The default group for every connector in a new policyUsable together only with other Non-Business connectors
BlockedKept from being used at allCannot be used in any flow or app in scope
  • Connectors in different groups cannot share data. With SharePoint in Business and Gmail in Non-Business, a maker cannot build a flow that uses both.
  • Cannot be blocked (classify as Business or Non-Business only): Dataverse, Approvals, Notifications and the Microsoft 365 enterprise standard connectors. All third-party connectors and all Microsoft premium connectors except Dataverse can be blocked.
  • HTTP is classifiable, but child flows depend on the HTTP connector, so its group can break child flows.
  • Create or edit a policy as Environment Admin or Power Platform admin: Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > + New Policy. A flow that violates a policy is suspended, its trigger does not fire, and the flow checker reports the violation.
  • Advanced connector policies use a strict allowlist (blocked unless allowed) for certified connectors only; custom and HTTP connectors still need classic data policies.

Connections and connection references

  • A connection stores the credential for one connector. A connection reference is a solution component that points to a connection. Operations in a solution-aware flow bind to connection references, not to connections; on import, a connection is supplied for each reference so the flows can turn on.
  • Create one: Solutions > open the solution > New > More > Connection Reference. Flows use references for all connectors; canvas apps only for implicitly shared (non-OAuth) connections such as SQL Server authentication.
SituationRecommend
No prebuilt connector exists for an internal REST APIA custom connector, with Premium or trial licenses for the users or a Process license for the flow
Hundreds of Microsoft 365 users start an instant flow that uses a premium connectorPut the flow in a solution and assign a Process license instead of licensing each user
Exam traps
  • Instant flows use the invoking user's license; automated and scheduled flows use the owner's. The owner's connection does not change the license check.
  • Premium is not custom. Dataverse is premium but cannot be blocked; Approvals is standard and cannot be blocked.
  • In a new policy every connector starts in Non-Business, not Business.

Manage approvals by using cloud flows

GA The Standard approvals connector (class Standard) provides Create an approval (does not wait), Start and wait for an approval, Wait for an approval (waits for a specified approval) and Start and wait for an approval of text. Older "Start and wait" variants are marked Deprecated. Approvals are stored in Dataverse; in a non-default environment the database is provisioned when the first approval flow runs, by a user with an administrator role.

Approval typeThe flow continues when
Approve/Reject - First to respondAny one approver approves or rejects
Approve/Reject - Everyone must approveAll approvers respond, or a single rejection occurs
Custom Responses - Wait for one responseAny one approver chooses one of your options
Custom Responses - Wait for all responsesAll approvers have responded with one of your options
Sequential approvalApprovers answer one at a time in a set order and the flow continues after all of them respond. The same approver cannot be assigned to two steps

The get-started page says "four approval types" but lists five.

  • Fields: approval type, Title, Assigned to, Details (Markdown supported), Item link and its description, Requestor, Enable notifications, Enable reassignment. The flow creator is always shown to approvers.
  • Outputs: Outcome, Responses (per approver, with comments) and a response summary. For the two Approve/Reject types the valid responses are Approve and Reject, and they are case-sensitive. Branch on Outcome with a Condition, or a Switch for custom responses.
  • Where approvers respond: an Outlook actionable message, the Approvals app in Teams, or Power Automate Action items > Approvals (Received tab; the requester sees Sent). Outlook and OWA actionable messages show only the first five custom responses. The standalone Power Automate mobile app is Deprecated since 2026-08-31.
  • Groups: only mail-enabled Microsoft 365 groups and security groups; one member's response stands for the group. With group 1 plus user 1, First to respond needs user 1 or one member of group 1; Everyone must approve needs user 1 and one member of group 1. Teams notifications are not supported for group approvals.
  • Guests cannot view or act on an approval by default; they need a valid Power Automate license and an accepted B2B invitation. Pending guests are removed, and if every approver is pending the creation fails. Users outside the environment get the Approvals User role automatically.
  • Reassign or cancel: an approver uses the three dots > Reassign. The requester cannot reassign: cancel the request on the Sent tab and edit Assigned to in the flow.
NeedUse
Do other work after sending and before waitingCreate an approval then Wait for an approval, close together; otherwise Start and wait for an approval
Ordered chain (manager, then finance)Sequential approval type, or Start and wait → Condition on Outcome → next approval in If yes
Independent approvers at the same timeParallel branches (Add a parallel branch), each with its own approval; the step after the branches runs when all finish

Timeouts, limits and reliability

  • The approvals known-issues page says an approval flow can wait 28 days; after that the flow fails and the approval stays in the action center until someone deletes it. The limits page gives a 30-day run duration after which pending steps time out. Design for decisions well inside that window.
  • If Create and Wait are separate actions and an approver answers before the flow reaches Wait for an approval, the flow can get stuck. Call the two close together, or change the approval status in Dataverse before the wait.
  • Do not evaluate approvals in a Do until loop. Use a Condition or Switch that covers every outcome. The final states of a basic approval are Approved, Rejected or Canceled.

Preview Multistage and AI approvals are available exclusively in agent flows built in Copilot Studio; they are not part of classic cloud flows.

Exam traps
  • Everyone must approve ends at the first rejection. Custom Responses - Wait for all responses waits for every approver.
  • Custom responses sent to many users with Everyone must approve can fail (results field size limit); Outlook shows only five custom buttons.
  • A guest assigned to an approval cannot act on it without a Power Automate license, and unaccepted invitations are dropped.
  • Splitting Create and Wait can hang the flow, and a Do until loop around an approval risks an endless loop.
  • Outcome values are Approve and Reject; the final approval states are Approved, Rejected and Canceled.

Configure cloud flow actions

GA Pick the right data operation, store values correctly, write expressions with exact function names and filter Dataverse data at the source. Prompt and AI model actions in flows are in §3.2.

ActionUse it toRemember
ComposeKeep one value or the result of an expression for reuseNo initialization; read with outputs('Compose')
SelectChange the shape of each object in an array: add, remove or rename propertiesCannot change the number of objects
Filter arrayReduce an array to the objects that match criteriaReturns fewer items; use Select to reshape
JoinTurn an array into one string with a separatorFields From and Join with
Create CSV table, Create HTML tableConvert a JSON array into a tableSelect IsHtml in the email action to send HTML
Parse JSONTurn a JSON string into structured data you can pick from dynamic contentNeeds a schema

Variables

  • Types: integer, float, boolean, string, array and object. Initialize variable creates one variable per action, only at the top level, not inside scopes, conditions or loops. Then use Set variable, Increment variable and Decrement variable (integer and float only), and Append to string variable or Append to array variable. Read with variables('name').
  • Inside an Apply to each that runs in parallel the results are unpredictable; keep such loops sequential.

Expressions (Workflow Definition Language)

NeedSyntax
Trigger outputtriggerOutputs() (shorthand for trigger().outputs) and triggerBody() (trigger().outputs.body)
Action output, loop itemoutputs('Get_item'), items('Apply_to_each'). Spaces in action names become underscores and names are case-sensitive
First non-null valuecoalesce(a, b, 'default'). Empty strings, empty arrays and empty objects are not null
Conditional valueif(equals(a, b), 'yes', 'no'); compare with equals, greater, less, greaterOrEquals, lessOrEquals; combine with and() and or()
Date and timeutcNow(), addDays(utcNow(), 7), formatDateTime(ts, 'yyyy-MM-dd'). MM is month and mm is minutes
Arrays and scopesfirst(array), join(array, ', '), empty(value); result('ScopeName') returns first-level actions only

Dataverse actions and OData

The Microsoft Dataverse connector (Premium) provides List rows, Get a row by ID, Add a new row, Update a row, Upsert a row (update if it exists, otherwise add), Delete a row, Relate rows / Unrelate rows (one-to-many or many-to-many links) and Perform a changeset request (one transaction: if one operation fails, the successful ones are rolled back).

List rows settingValue and rule
Select columnsComma-separated, for example name,emailaddress1
Filter rowsOData filter, for example statecode eq 0 or createdon ge 2021-01-01T00:00:00-00:00. No $filter= prefix; URL-encode &, # and +
Sort by, Row countname desc (ascending is the default); the number of rows Dataverse should return
Expand QueryRelated-table data, for example primarycontactid($select=contactid,fullname) (the page also shows primarycontactid(contactid,fullname))
Fetch Xml QueryFetchXML; no aggregation; the pagination setting does not apply
  1. Without pagination the page limit is 5,000 rows; to return more, open the action Settings and turn Pagination on.
  2. Set Threshold to the rows you need (maximum 100,000). It is rounded up in steps of the page size, so 7,000 with a 5,000 page size returns 10,000.
  3. With FetchXML, manage paging inside the query instead.

Action settings and child flows

  • Action settings: Timeout (ISO 8601 duration such as PT5M), Retry policy, Run after, concurrency control. A retry policy resends on 408, 429 and 5xx (exponential is preferred): default up to two retries for the Low performance profile or 12 for Medium and High; at most 90 retries; delays from 5 seconds to 1 day.
  • Child flows must be in a solution, start with Manually trigger a flow, and are called with Run a Child Flow. Parent connections cannot be passed; child flows use embedded connections.
  • Create with Copilot on the Home page builds a first draft: describe the flow in What will your flow do?, select Keep it and continue, then Create flow.
Exam traps
  • Typing $filter= into Filter rows breaks the action. The same rule applies to the Dataverse trigger.
  • coalesce() does not skip empty strings, and mm is minutes while MM is the month.
  • Pagination threshold is rounded to page-size steps, and it is ignored for FetchXML.
  • Initialize variable inside a loop, scope or condition is not allowed; Increment variable on a string is not allowed.
  • Select keeps the item count; Filter array changes it.

Implement flow control with conditions and loops

GA Flow control decides which actions run, how often and in what order.

ControlUse it whenKey facts
ConditionTwo paths and any comparison, including greater thanIf yes and If no branches; Add builds AND/OR groups; Edit in advanced mode shows the expression. Comparisons are case-sensitive; trailing spaces and 1 versus "1" also break them
SwitchMany discrete values of one fieldEquality only. Needs at least one case plus Default; case values must be unique static values, not tokens or expressions. Maximum 25 cases
Apply to eachProcess every item of an arraySequential by default. Concurrency control: degree 1 to 50, top-level loop only (inner loops run sequentially). Array limit 5,000 (Low profile) or 100,000 (others)
Do untilRepeat until a condition is trueStops at the Count limit (default 60, maximum 5,000) or the Timeout (default PT1H, ISO 8601), whichever comes first. A running iteration is not cut off
ScopeGroup actions for tidiness and error handlingOne aggregate status; the Try/Catch pattern
TerminateEnd the run on purposeSet a status (for example Failed) and message; stops in-progress actions and skips the rest
Parallel branchesIndependent steps (for example, over five seconds each)The flow continues only after all branches finish

Configure run after and Try/Catch

  • An action can run after the previous action succeeded (default), failed, was skipped or timed out. Open the action Settings > Run after and tick Has failed or Has timed out; clear the default Is successful to run only on failure. The setting does not exist on the first action. An unhandled failure marks the action Failed and its successors Skipped.
  1. Put the main actions in a Try scope.
  2. Add a Catch scope and set its run after on Try to Has failed (and Has timed out).
  3. In Catch, use a Filter array whose input is result('Try') to isolate the failed action, then log or notify.
  4. Finish with Terminate (status Failed) so the run does not look successful.
RequirementUse
Branch on Status = New, Open or Closed (Amount greater than 1000 needs a Condition)Switch
500 independent rows, no shared variables, run fasterApply to each with concurrency control (up to 50)
Counter or running total inside a loopKeep the loop sequential and use Increment variable
Poll an API for at most 30 minutesDo until with Timeout PT30M; raise Count if more than 60 checks are needed
Notify the team only when an action failsRun after = Has failed on the notification action
Exam traps
  • Trigger concurrency (how many runs at once) and Apply to each concurrency (how many iterations at once) are different settings.
  • Raising only the Do until Count (or only the Timeout) does not help; the first limit reached ends the loop.
  • Switch cannot test greater than, and its case values cannot be dynamic content.
  • Ticking only Has failed means the action is skipped when the previous action succeeds.
  • Limits: nesting depth 8, 500 actions per flow, 25 Switch cases.

Test and troubleshoot cloud flows

GA Work in this order: flow checker, test, run history, fix, resubmit.

  • Flow checker: the stethoscope icon on the designer command bar; it also opens when you save a flow with errors or warnings, shows the fix in red on the action, and reports data policy violations.
  • Test: save first. Manually means you perform the trigger action. Automatically reuses a recently used trigger or repeats a previous test run, and is available only after at least one manual test.
  • Static result (mock data): select the action, open the Testing tab and switch Static result on, pasting the body copied from Show raw outputs of a real run. The action counts as successful without running (beaker icon). Typical use: test the branches after Start and wait for an approval without sending requests.

Run history and error codes

  1. Open the flow and select the failed run in the 28-day run history.
  2. Open the red step and read How to fix.
  3. For 401 or 403, select View Connections and then Fix connection next to the broken connection.
  4. Return to the failed run and select Resubmit.
Code or messageMeaningFix
401, 403, UnauthorizedAuthentication problemView Connections > Fix connection, then Resubmit
400 Bad request, 404 Not foundAn action setting does not workCorrect the action, save, then Resubmit
500, 502Temporary failureResubmit
  • Resubmit and cancel: up to 20 runs at once (All runs). Users can always resubmit their own instant-trigger runs; for runs started by others an admin must enable Power Automate flow run resubmission in the Power Platform admin center. Resubmitting can duplicate records or emails.
  • Automatic turn-off: continuous failures for 14 days; consistent throttling for 14 days (a Process license gives dedicated capacity); 90 days without a trigger. Flows owned by Premium-licensed users or with a Process license are not subject to the 90-day suspension.
  • Notifications: a per-run failure alert is sent only for known fixable causes (such as a broken connection or a throttled action) to the owner and co-owners, never to run-only users or admins, with a 28-day cooldown per flow. A weekly digest lists all failures; admins use Monitor in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Solution flows can also keep run history in the Dataverse FlowRun table (28 days by default).
  • Copilot: in the new designer, Copilot can help find and fix errors (Troubleshoot in Copilot).
Exam traps
  • Automatic testing is not available until a manual test has run once, and a flow must be saved before it can be tested.
  • 401 and 403 need Fix connection; 400 and 404 need an action change; a retry policy only helps transient errors such as 408, 429 and 5xx.
  • Resubmit is not a safe default: it can create duplicate rows or send duplicate emails.
  • A static result skips the real action, so it proves the branches work, not the connector.
