sections.title: 3.2 Create prompts and models in AI Hub
sections.html:
Skills measured: Build prompts from templates or from blank • Consume a prompt in apps • Consume a prompt in cloud flows • Add knowledge to a prompt • Customize prompt settings, including models • Add inputs to a prompt • Consume an AI model in apps • Consume an AI model in cloud flows. Build one prompt from a template and one from blank, call each from a canvas app and a cloud flow, then call a prebuilt and a published custom AI model the same way.

Build prompts from templates or from blank

GA The AI hub is a left-navigation item in Power Apps and Power Automate. If it is not pinned, select ... More > AI hub, then under Discover an AI capability choose Prompts or AI models (the pin icon keeps the hub on the menu). AI Builder is still the feature name behind both. The hub's Monitor activity area (Power Automate Automation center > Monitor > AI Builder activity) shows model and prompt runs from Power Apps, Power Automate and Copilot Studio. Copilot Studio has no AI hub: the same prompt builder appears there as a tool (Tools > New tool > Prompt).

Starting pointHowUse when
Blank promptAI hub > Prompts > Build your own promptYou write your own instructions and add your own inputs and knowledge
Prompt template (prompt library)Build your own prompt > Start from a prompt template, or Popular templates / See all templatesThe job is a standard one; you edit the starter text and save it under your own name
Prompt assistantDescribe the intent (4-500 characters), select Submit, then Keep itYou have only an intent sentence and want a first draft
  • The library filters by job type (Common, Customer service, Legal, Marketing, Communications, Information technology, Learning, HR, Finance, Architecture, Sales) and by task (Analyze, Classify, Create, Extract, Summarize). The library cannot be shown inside a canvas app or a flow: save the prompt, then call the saved prompt.
  • The prompt assistant (renamed from Create a prompt with Copilot) writes new drafts only. It cannot improve an existing prompt and cannot create grounded prompts, that is, prompts that use knowledge.
  • Creating a prompt needs Environment Maker, System Customizer or System Administrator; Basic User cannot create prompts or models. Prompts live in Dataverse, and an admin can switch the feature off per environment (the AI prompts setting, on by default).
  • Testing in the prompt builder is free. A new prompt is private until it is shared as User (run it) or Co-owner (run, edit, share, delete).

Steps

  1. Open AI hub > Prompts and select Build your own prompt, or start from a template.
  2. Name the prompt (select the generated name at the top left).
  3. Write or edit the instructions: an instruction plus the context the model needs.
  4. Add inputs and knowledge with / or Add content, and give each input a sample value.
  5. Pick the model and settings, then select Test.
  6. Save the prompt, Share it if others must run it, and call it from an app, a flow or an agent.
Exam traps
  • Four different things share the word "prompt": a template (editable starter), a prebuilt prompt such as AISummarize (fixed Microsoft text), a prompt column (§1.2) and a prompt tool in Copilot Studio.
  • The prompt assistant limit is 4-500 characters, and it cannot improve a prompt that already exists.
  • A Basic User cannot create a prompt. Running one only needs the prompt to be shared with the user.
  • Some pages still show old paths such as AI Hub > AI prompts or Library > Add an Item > New Action > Prompt. The current path is AI hub > Prompts.

Consume a prompt in apps

GA To consume a saved prompt in a canvas app, select Data > + Add data and pick the prompt. It then works as a Power Fx function: call .Predict on its name and pass the prompt's input.

// Button.OnSelect
Set( result, 'Ticket summarizer'.Predict( txtTicket.Text ) )

Show the returned text in a label. Run the prompt from OnSelect and keep the result in a variable, because every run consumes credits (testing in the prompt builder is free).

Prebuilt prompts: AI functions

For common tasks you can skip authoring. Add the Environment data source and pass one record of named columns; the result is a one-column record. These are behavior functions, so call them in a behavior property such as OnSelect and store the result with Set.

Set( Summary, Environment.AISummarize( { Text: txtNotes.Text } ).SummarizedText )
FunctionArgumentsOutput column
AISummarizeTextSummarizedText
AIClassifyText, CategoriesClassification
AIReplyTextPreparedResponse
AISentimentTextAnalyzedSentiment (Positive, Neutral or Negative)
AITranslateText, TargetLanguageTranslatedText

AIExtract and AISummarizeRecord also exist; the AI functions page describes AIExtract as still in development.

NeedUse
Your own instructions, inputs or knowledgeA saved prompt: Add data, then 'Name'.Predict(...)
A common task with nothing to authorAn AI function through the Environment data source
A fixed analysis such as language, sentiment or invoice fieldsA prebuilt AI model, also called with .Predict (see the AI model sections)
AI text stored on every row in a model-driven appA prompt column (§1.2)
  • Model-driven apps: the documented ways to surface AI text are a prompt column (§1.2) and the Dataverse low-code plug-in that calls prebuilt prompts such as AISummarize, which is Preview. The .Predict pattern above is the canvas app pattern.
  • Share the prompt with everyone who runs the app (User); sharing the app does not share the prompt. Building an app that calls a prompt needs Environment Maker or higher.
  • Prompts are Dataverse-backed and solution-aware: in a solution use Add existing > AI models and export as managed (§1.1).
  • Running a prompt uses AI Builder credits first, then Copilot Credits. An app that uses an AI Builder action is a premium app.
  • A prompt used as a tool in a Copilot Studio agent cannot take image or document inputs, and an agent that allows anonymous users cannot use Dataverse knowledge.
Exam traps
  • .Predict serves saved prompts and AI models; Environment.AIxxx( {...} ) serves the prebuilt prompts; a bare AIxxx(text) is the form used outside canvas apps.
  • An AI function in a label's Text property fails: it is a behavior function. Use Set in OnSelect and show the variable.
  • If a saved prompt or model is not listed in Add data, check that it is shared with the maker.
  • OnChange re-runs the prompt and re-bills it; use a button's OnSelect.

Consume a prompt in cloud flows

GA Use the Run a prompt action. Since May 2025 this is the name of the action formerly called Create text with GPT using a prompt; some AI Builder pages still show the old name. The older text generation model and its Create text with GPT action are Deprecated. In an agent flow, find the action under AI capabilities > Run a prompt.

  1. Create an instant cloud flow with the Manually trigger a flow trigger, or any trigger that supplies the input.
  2. Add Run a prompt, choose the saved prompt in the Prompt list (or New custom prompt to build one inside the flow), and map each prompt input with dynamic content.
  3. Use the Text output in later actions.
  4. For human review add Start and wait for an approval of text (§3.1) and set Suggested Text to Text.
  5. Add a Condition where Outcome is equal to Approve, and post the accepted text in the True branch.
Prompt output formatWhat later actions receive
Text (default)The Text output, a single string
JSONEach JSON element becomes dynamic content; the format is locked when the prompt is saved
Document PreviewDocument Output Content Bytes, for example as the File content of a OneDrive Create file action

Token counts are available in expressions on the action's output:

outputs('Run_a_prompt')?['body/responsev2/predictionOutput/promptTokens']
outputs('Run_a_prompt')?['body/responsev2/predictionOutput/completionTokens']
  • Input tokens include a system metaprompt of about 1,200 tokens plus your instructions, inputs and retrieved knowledge.
  • Classic flows consume AI Builder credits first, then Copilot Credits; agent flows consume Copilot Credits only. A basic, standard or premium model costs 0.1, 1.5 or 10 Copilot Credits per 1,000 tokens.
  • Start with the Basic model and add only the data the prompt needs.
  • The flow runner needs the prompt shared with them. AI Builder actions belong to the Dataverse connector in DLP policies, so a policy that splits Dataverse and Outlook into different groups blocks emailing AI output.
Exam traps
  • Run a prompt is the renamed Create text with GPT using a prompt; it is not the deprecated Create text with GPT action.
  • To use fields from a result in later steps, choose JSON output; Text output is one string.
  • Document output is Preview. Sharing the flow does not share the prompt.
  • Agent flows always use Copilot Credits; classic flows use AI Builder credits first.

Add knowledge to a prompt

GA Knowledge grounds a prompt in business data (retrieval-augmented generation): besides the model's training data, the prompt receives the rows you select. The documented sources are Dataverse tables and, only for prompts that run in Power Automate, connector tables (for example Salesforce, Oracle and Zendesk).

  1. In the instructions type / or select Add content, and pick a data source object from the Knowledge section.
  2. Select the columns to use.
  3. Select the knowledge object, choose Filter attribute (the column) and enter a Filter value: free text or a prompt input.
  4. Select Insert and navigate the data and relationships to add references to related tables into the instructions.
  5. Open ... > Settings to change Record retrieval and Include links in the response (link citations for the retrieved records), then Test and Save.
LimitValue
Records retrieved30 by default; raise to a maximum of 1,000 with Record retrieval
Dataverse relationshipsOne-to-many or many-to-one only, up to two levels from the table you add
Virtual tablesNot supported
Filter attribute data typesText, number, date and time, choice, currency, unique identifier
Connector sourcesOnly for prompts used in Power Automate
Copilot Studio agentsAn agent that allows anonymous users (no authentication) cannot use Dataverse tables as knowledge
The prompt needs...Use
Rows from Dataverse that it looks up, such as an account's ordersKnowledge, filtered by an input
A value or a file supplied when the prompt runsA Text or Image or document input
A value computed when the prompt runs, such as a dateA Power Fx input

Knowledge counts as input tokens, so filter the rows and keep only the columns you need.

Exam traps
  • The numbers: 30 records by default, 1,000 maximum, two relationship levels, one-to-many or many-to-one only, no virtual tables.
  • Knowledge (rows the prompt retrieves) is not an input (a value passed at run time). An input often feeds the knowledge Filter value.
  • Connector knowledge works only when the prompt runs in Power Automate; a canvas app that calls the prompt cannot use it.
  • The prompt assistant cannot create grounded prompts, so add knowledge in the editor.

Customize prompt settings, including models

GA Choose the model in the Model list at the top of the prompt builder. Open the settings panel with the three dots (...) > Settings.

SettingWhat it doesRemember
Temperature0 is deterministic, 1 is more creativeRange 0-1; default 0; the slider is disabled for GPT-5 reasoning
Record retrievalNumber of records retrieved for knowledge30 by default, up to 1,000
Include links in the responseAdds link citations for retrieved recordsThe records come from the prompt's knowledge
Enable code interpreterGenerates and runs code; Word, Excel and PowerPoint files become usable as inputsNot supported in sovereign clouds
Content moderation levelLow, Moderate or High filtering of harmful contentDefault Moderate; managed models only, unavailable for Anthropic and Azure AI Foundry models

Choose Low moderation for prompts that process data that could count as harmful content, such as descriptions of violence or medical procedures; High filters more strictly than Moderate and returns fewer answers.

ModelRateCategoryStatus
GPT-4.1 mini (default model)BasicMiniGA
GPT-4.1StandardGeneralGA
GPT-5 chatStandardGeneralGA
GPT-5 reasoningPremiumDeepGA
GPT-5.2 reasoningPremiumDeepExperimental, US only
GPT-5.3 chatStandardGeneralExperimental, US only
Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6Standard, PremiumGeneral, DeepExperimental, even when no tag is shown
Grok 4.1 Fast (Non-reasoning)StandardGeneralExperimental; not recommended for production
  • The default model is periodically upgraded and is the fallback when a selected model is turned off or unavailable. Categories: Mini is fast and good for most tasks, General suits complex tasks, Deep reasons first and is slower.
  • Retired: o3 on December 4, 2025 (replacement GPT-5 reasoning); GPT-4o mini and GPT-4o in July 2025 (replacements GPT-4.1 mini and GPT-4.1); o1 in July 2025 (replacement o3). The US government clouds GCC and GCC High keep GPT-4o mini, GPT-4.1 mini and GPT-4o as GA.
  • Prompts that use models consume Copilot Credits whatever the release stage; AI Builder credits are used first in Power Apps and Power Automate, never in Copilot Studio.
  • GPT-5 chat and GPT-5 reasoning are available in-region only in Europe and the United States; in other regions they are marked GA (cross-geo), meaning data may be processed outside your region. The Move data across regions setting (the environment's Generative AI features card) governs cross-geography processing.
Output formatNotes
TextDefault
JSONAuto detected or Custom; the format is locked when you save. For the error "A JSON could not be generated" add "Don't include JSON markdown in your answer" to the instructions
Document PreviewFills a Word layout of up to 20 MB that uses {{FieldName}} placeholders without spaces

Bring your own model (Azure AI Foundry)

  • In the Model list choose Connect a model from Azure AI Foundry and enter the Model deployment name and Base model name exactly as in Foundry.
  • The deployment must use the chat completions endpoint; the Responses API fails with "Resource not found". The GPT-5 family and later are not supported.
  • DLP policies treat it as the Azure AI Foundry connector, and the moderation slider does not apply.
  • Admin switches (Power Platform admin center > Environments > the environment > Settings > Product > Features, all on by default): AI prompts, Preview and experimental AI models (formerly the AI Builder preview models setting) and External models.
  • Test hub Preview (the three dots next to the prompt) runs batches of test cases, scored by Response quality, Response matches or JSON correctness against a Passing score.
Exam traps
  • The default model is GPT-4.1 mini, not GPT-4o. Some pages still mention GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini or o3, which are retired.
  • Content moderation is unavailable for Claude and Foundry models; temperature is disabled for GPT-5 reasoning.
  • Claude models are experimental even though no tag is shown. Experimental models are not for production.
  • BYOM needs a chat completions deployment and cannot use the GPT-5 family.
  • The JSON format is locked on save, so decide Auto detected or Custom before saving.

Add inputs to a prompt

GA Inputs let an app, flow or agent supply values when the prompt runs. In the instructions type / or select Add content, then choose an input type in the Input section. Rename it in Name, reference it in the instruction text, and give it Sample data so that you can Test the prompt.

Input typeUse forDetails
TextText to summarize, classify, extract from or analyzeDefault name Text input
Image or documentA picture or file to summarize, categorize, extract from or ask questions aboutDefault name Document input; PNG, JPG, JPEG, PDF; can be combined with text inputs
Power FxA value computed at run time: current date, text formatting or search, calculationsAny function not related to connectors; read other inputs as Input.'Your input name'
Text( Now(), Input.'Date Format' )
  • Files: all files together under 25 MB, documents under 50 pages, processing capped at 100 seconds. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files are accepted only when code interpreter is on.
  • Inputs cannot contain instructions (a security restriction); keep the instructions in the prompt text.
  • Image tokens: an image under 512 x 512 costs 85 tokens; a larger image is resized and split into 512 x 512 tiles at 170 tokens each plus 85 base tokens. Each PDF page is converted to an image.
  • Where inputs surface: each input is a field of Run a prompt in a flow and an argument of .Predict in a canvas app. Image or document inputs are not yet supported on prompts used as tools in Copilot Studio agents.
Exam traps
  • There are three input types: Text, Image or document, Power Fx. Knowledge is not an input type.
  • 25 MB is the combined size of all files, not per file; the page limit is under 50 pages.
  • A Power Fx input cannot call connector functions, and a Text input does not evaluate a formula.
  • Excel and Word files need code interpreter; PDF, PNG, JPG and JPEG do not.

Consume an AI model in apps

GA AI hub > AI models lists prebuilt models (ready to use) and custom models (you train, publish and share). To consume a model in a canvas app, call it in a formula or insert an AI Builder component.

KindModels
PrebuiltBusiness card reader, ID reader, invoice processing, receipt processing, text recognition, key phrase extraction, language detection, sentiment analysis, text translation. Category classification and entity extraction also have a standard model; the model types page tags the prebuilt category classification model as preview
Custom (train, publish, share)Document processing, prediction, object detection, category classification, entity extraction
Prebuilt, PreviewImage description, contract processing, health insurance card
DeprecatedText generation (GPT) model, replaced by prompts

Power Fx

Select Data > Add data > AI models and add the model (a model that is not listed has not been shared with you). Call .Predict on its name from a button's OnSelect, not OnChange, and keep the result in a variable.

Set( lang, 'Language detection'.Predict( txtReview.Text ).Language )
ModelCallResult record
Language detection'Language detection'.Predict(Text)Language, Confidence
Sentiment analysis'Sentiment analysis'.Predict(Text)Document (AllSentiments, TopSentiment), Sentences
Key phrase extraction'Key phrase extraction'.Predict(Text)Phrases
Category classification'Category classification'.Predict(Text)AllClasses, TopClass
Entity extraction (custom)'Model name'.Predict(Text)Entities (Type, Value, StartIndex, Length, Confidence)
Invoice processing'Invoice processing'.Predict(UploadedImage1.Image)Fields, for example .Fields.InvoiceId.Value.Text
Object detection (custom)'Model name'.Predict(Image)Objects (Name, Confidence, BoundingBox)

AI Builder components

Component (Insert > AI Builder)ModelNotes
Business card reader, Receipt processor, Text recognizerPrebuiltNothing to train
Form processor (document processor), Object detectorCustom, publishedForm processor confidence colors: red 0-39, orange 40-59, blue 60-100. The object detector returns GroupedResults (TagId, TagName, ObjectCount)
  • Model-driven apps: add the AI Builder Business Card control to a form, bound to a text column. A Basic User is enough, and the Company Name field cannot be bound to the Lookup.Customer field. A prediction model shows its results in predicted columns of a view.
  • Roles: Environment Maker or higher creates models and the apps or flows that call them. A Basic User runs apps that use models they own or that are shared with them. A model is private until shared: User can see and run it; Co-owner can edit, retrain, publish and share it but cannot delete it. Sharing the app does not share the model.
  • Schema-changing models: publishing a prediction model for the first time needs at least System Customizer, because a column is added to the input table. A category classification model creates a Dataverse table when it first runs, so only a System Customizer or System Administrator can run it at first; an administrator must then change access to the new table so that users can see the results.
  • Lifecycle and ALM: a custom model moves from draft through training and trained to published. Up to two trained versions are kept, and publishing overwrites the earlier published version. Solutions carry only the published version and no training data; imported document processing, object detection and entity extraction models cannot be retrained. After moving an app to another environment, re-add the model (§1.1).
  • Data and licence: models run in the environment's region and images or documents sent for prediction are not stored. An app that uses an AI Builder action is a premium app. The business card reader and prediction models are free; other models consume credits.
Exam traps
  • A custom model appears in Add data or in a component only when it is published and shared.
  • Custom document processing in a canvas app uses the form processor component; prebuilt invoice, receipt and ID models are called with .Predict.
  • A category classification result is TopClass; a language detection result is Language. Do not mix the shapes.
  • A model co-owner cannot delete the model, while a prompt co-owner can delete the prompt.

Consume an AI model in cloud flows

GA To consume a model in a cloud flow, add an AI Builder action (+ New step > AI Builder), pick the model or document type, map the input and use the output fields. The flow owner must be able to use the model, so share it first.

CapabilityAction name
Sentiment analysisAnalyze positive or negative sentiment in text
Category classificationClassify text into categories with one of your custom models / with the standard model
Language detectionDetect the language being used in the text
Entity extractionExtract entities from text with one of your custom models / with the standard model
Business card, identity document, invoice, receiptExtract information from business cards / identity documents / invoices / receipts
Custom document processingProcess documents (formerly Extract information from documents)
Key phrase extractionGenerate the key phrases from a text
Image description PreviewGenerate description of an image
PredictionPredict whether something will happen by field / by record ID
Text recognitionRecognize text in an image or a PDF document
Text translationTranslate text into another language
PromptRun a prompt (formerly Create text with GPT using a prompt)
  • Process documents: inputs are AI Model (a trained, published model), Document type (PDF, JPEG or PNG), Form (the file) and an optional Pages value under Advanced parameters (1 or 3-5; the range should hold one unique form). Outputs are {field} value and {field} confidence score; table columns come back as {table}{column} value, so loop with Apply to each.
  • Predict: search for predict and choose Predict from AI Builder or Predict using AI Builder models from Microsoft Dataverse (both offer the same features), then select the custom or prebuilt model. The Predict page states that the dynamic model ID is supported only for document processing and not for prompts.
  • Asynchronous Pattern: leave this action setting On (the default) for every AI Builder action. If it is off, the output is JSON that starts with statusCode: 202 and the next action fails with "Unable to process template language expressions". Enable the setting and run the flow again.
  • Credits: classic flows consume AI Builder credits first, then Copilot Credits; agent flows consume Copilot Credits only. Creating, training and testing are free. Example: 3 pages of custom document processing in an agent flow cost 3 × 8 = 24 Copilot Credits. The business card reader and prediction are free.
  • Governance: AI Builder actions belong to the Dataverse connector in DLP policies. Scheduled prediction runs and retraining are Preview.

Steps

  1. Publish and share the model (custom models) and confirm that the flow owner can use it.
  2. Create the flow and its trigger.
  3. Add the AI Builder action (or Predict) and choose the model or document type.
  4. Map the file or text input; set Pages if only some pages matter.
  5. Use the output fields, looping with Apply to each for tables.
  6. Keep Asynchronous Pattern on, then save and Test.
Exam traps
  • Old and new names are mixed in the docs: Run a prompt, Process documents and the two names of Predict. The AI Builder action table still lists Create text with GPT using a prompt.
  • Output containing statusCode: 202 means the Asynchronous Pattern setting is off, not that the model needs retraining or resharing.
  • Document processing in a flow needs a trained and published model; solutions do not carry training data.
  • Agent flows use Copilot Credits only, and the business card reader and prediction are free.

sections.title: 3.3 Implement business and process logic
sections.html:
Skills measured: Configure business rules • Configure business process flows • Configure calculated, rollup, and formula columns • Evaluate use cases for business logic. Build one business rule in each scope, one business process flow with a required step and a branch, one calculated, one rollup and one formula column, and then pick the right tool for ten different requirements.

Configure business rules

GA A business rule is a no-code if/then designer (it is not Power Fx) for logic on the columns of one table. The scope decides where the rule runs, so it is the most tested setting. Forms are covered in §2.1 and canvas apps in §2.2.

ScopeRunsChoose it when
Table (labelled Entity in the designer; the default)Client side on the model-driven forms and server side when data changesThe rule must also hold for canvas apps, cloud flows and Dataverse API writes. Canvas apps must use this scope.
All FormsClient side only: the main and quick create formsForm behaviour that is the same on every form
One specific formClient side only: that formBehaviour for a single form
  • Server side: conditions are evaluated when the row is saved, in the pre-operation stage of the database transaction. Show Error Message cancels the save, rolls the transaction back and returns the message to the caller. The server part is generated XAML that runs as a synchronous plug-in. Actions that exist only for model-driven apps are ignored when the rule runs on the server.
  • Client side: a rule runs when a form opens and when a referenced column changes, before onLoad scripts. Saving or editing a rule does not re-run it on existing rows.
  • To fire on a form, the column must be on the form and the user needs at least user-level Read on the Process table (the Basic User role has it).
ActionWhat it doesAvailability
Set Field ValueSets a fixed value, another column or a "simple formula" (add, subtract, multiply or divide two columns); can also clear a valueAll scopes, canvas apps included
Set Default ValueSets the value only when the column is emptyAll scopes, canvas apps included
Show Error MessageBlocks the save and shows the messageAll scopes, canvas apps included
Set Business RequiredSets the requirement level on the form: Business Required (red asterisk, blocks the save while empty) or OptionalModel-driven forms. Microsoft Learn calls requirement-level actions form-scope actions, but its canvas-app limitation lists do not name this one, so do not rely on it outside model-driven forms. It is a user-interface rule: Dataverse itself does not reject an empty Business Required column
Set VisibilityShows or hides a columnModel-driven forms only; not canvas apps
Lock or UnlockMakes a column read-only or editableModel-driven forms only; not canvas apps
RecommendationShows a suggestion; accepting it can set column valuesModel-driven only; not canvas apps; cannot be created for table-based view pages
  • Conditions: every rule starts with a condition (if-then-else). Actions go on the check-mark (true) path or the X (false) path. Add clauses with New on the Properties tab and set Rule Logic to AND or OR.
  • Limits: 150 business rules per table, client and server rules together. Not supported: multi-select Choices, File and Language columns, plus unique identifier, rollup, localizable-value and composite columns such as Full Name. Rules see only the columns of their own table (no rows through 1:N or N:1 relationships) and cannot change tabs or sections. DateOnly columns are evaluated in UTC, so use the Time Zone Independent behavior.
  • Not covered: editable subgrids and Power Pages basic forms do not support business rules. Business rule or code: JavaScript is needed for tabs, sections, subgrids or related rows, a cloud flow for cross-system or after-save work, and a plug-in only when declarative options cannot meet the requirement.

Steps

  1. Tables > open the table > Business rules > Add business rule.
  2. Add a description and set the scope (Entity/Table is the default).
  3. Set the properties of the condition that is already on the canvas, then select Apply. There is no autosave.
  4. Drag actions to the plus sign beside the check mark or the X, set their properties and select Apply.
  5. Select Validate, then Save.
  6. Close the designer, select the rule in the list and select Activate. A rule cannot be activated from the designer, and an active rule must be deactivated before it is edited.
Exam traps
  • All Forms is client only. Only Table (Entity) scope also runs on the server, so it is the only scope that covers canvas apps, cloud flows and API writes.
  • Set Visibility, Lock/Unlock and Recommendation are model-driven only: not available in canvas apps, and ignored when a rule runs on the server.
  • Show Error Message with Table scope rejects the save from any channel; Set Business Required is a model-driven form action and is ignored when the rule runs on the server.
  • A rule that does not fire usually has a column missing from the form, was never activated, or the user lacks Read on the Process table. Rules are not retroactive.
  • The 150-rule ceiling counts client and server rules together, per table.

Configure business process flows

GA A business process flow (BPF) guides users through stages and steps at the top of a model-driven app form and can gate progress with required steps. It is guidance, not background automation, and it works only in model-driven apps. A business rule or form script that sets or hides a column is reflected in the BPF control. Table and role basics are in §1.2.

LimitValue
Active BPFs per table10
Process instances on one row (one per BPF definition)10
Stages per process30
Steps per stage30
Tables in a multi-table process5
Branching depth10 levels (an older branching article says 5)
  • Create: in a solution, New > Automation > Process > Business process flow (steps below). The primary table cannot be changed after the first save. Creating BPFs from the Power Automate area outside a solution was removed in August 2022.
  • Components: Stage, Step, Condition, Workflow (a classic on-demand workflow), Action and Flow. A Learn training unit still calls the Flow step preview.
  • Stage: display name, Category (the global choice processstage_category: Qualify, Develop, Propose, Close, Identify, Research, Resolve, Approval), a table (changeable on every stage except the first) and, when the previous stage is on another table, a Relationship that must be 1:N.
  • Step: a column plus a Required flag. A required step blocks Next Stage until the column has a value. A required Two Options (Yes/No) column must be Yes; use a Choice column when either answer is acceptable. A hidden column does not block navigation; a disabled one still does.
  • Condition (branching): an if-else tile whose true and false outcomes each need a stage. Rules combine with AND or OR but not both, must be based on the immediately preceding stage. A table relationship is optional, but one you select must be 1:N. Peer branches must all merge into one stage or all end the process. Branching exposes later stage names even where table security hides the data, so use separate BPFs for confidential stages.
  • Workflow component: on a stage it fires on Stage Entry or Stage Exit; on the Global Workflow it fires when the process is completed or abandoned. A workflow on Stage Exit of the last stage never fires, so use the Global Workflow.
  • Activate: Validate > Save > Activate. A draft BPF cannot be used. Activating needs the prvActivateBusinessProcessFlow privilege on the Workflow table. Creating a BPF needs a per-user Power Apps or Power Automate licence, or a Dynamics 365 licence with BPF rights.
  • Security: a new BPF is visible only to System Administrator and System Customizer. Select Edit Security Roles (the article also calls it Enable Security Roles) and use the Business Process Flows tab of each role to grant it. Order Process Flow sets which active BPF a new row gets (the first one the user's role can access); users can change it with Switch Process.
  • BPF table: activation creates a custom table named <publisherprefix>_<uniquename> that stores the instances (activestageid, traversedpath). Only System Administrator and System Customizer can use it until you grant privileges. Add it to the solution manually before export. Selecting Business process flows (fields will be created) on a custom table cannot be undone.
  • In the app: the modern app designer has an Automation pane for the BPFs that belong to the app.

Steps

  1. Solutions > the solution > New > Automation > Process > Business process flow; enter the display name, name and table, then Create.
  2. Add Stage components (name, category) and Step components (column, Required), selecting Apply each time.
  3. Add a Condition between stages if the path branches.
  4. Validate, Save, Activate.
  5. Use Edit Security Roles (Business Process Flows tab) and Order Process Flow.

BPF or something else? Use a BPF for human-paced, staged data entry with gating. Use a cloud flow (§3.1) for background automation and a business rule for column-level behaviour. A BPF cannot advance itself when data changes: use the client API (formContext.data.process.moveNext) or update the instance row. Use one BPF with branches when the paths share a start and rejoin; use separate BPFs for concurrent processes, different roles or confidential stages, and for more than five tables.

Exam traps
  • Limits to remember: 10 active BPFs per table, 5 tables, 30 stages, 30 steps per stage.
  • A required Yes/No step is complete only when the answer is Yes; a business required column on a form treats No as a value.
  • A draft BPF is unusable, and a new BPF is hidden from everyone except System Administrator and System Customizer.
  • Branch rules use AND or OR, never both, and look only at the preceding stage.
  • A BPF is not a cloud flow. Stage Exit on the last stage never fires.

Configure calculated, rollup, and formula columns

GA All three create a derived, read-only value. They differ in when the value is computed and how far they can reach. Column basics are in §1.2.

CalculatedRollupFormula
CreateNew column > Behavior = Calculated > Save and edit > Behavior: EditNew column > Behavior = Rollup > edit the definitionNew column > Data type = fx Formula
AuthoringCONDITION and ACTION editor with uppercase functionsSource table, Related table (filters), AggregatePower Fx expression
ComputedOn retrieve (real time)By scheduled system jobs; the value is storedOn retrieve (real time)
ReachThis row and one parent through a lookup (two tables at most)Child rows over a 1:N relationshipThis row and related-table columns
Output typesText, Choice, Yes/No, Whole, Decimal, Currency, Date TimeWhole, Decimal, Currency, Date and timeText, Decimal, Whole, Float, Yes/No, Choice, DateTime; no Currency
Key limitsChain of 5; 50 unique per view or chartSUM, COUNT, MIN, MAX, AVG; no N:N; no rollup over rollup1,000 characters; depth 10; no self reference or cycles
Triggers a workflowNo (nor a plug-in)No; cannot be a wait conditionNo (nor a plug-in)
  • Calculated functions are uppercase: ADDDAYS, ADDHOURS, ADDWEEKS, ADDMONTHS, ADDYEARS, the matching SUBTRACT functions, DIFFINDAYS, DIFFINHOURS, DIFFINMINUTES, DIFFINMONTHS, DIFFINWEEKS, DIFFINYEARS, CONCAT, TRIMLEFT and TRIMRIGHT. TRIMLEFT("RXX10-3456789", 3) returns 10-3456789. Both columns in a DIFF function need the same behavior (User Local, Date Only or Time-Zone Independent).
  • Parent columns are read as ParentAccountId.AccountNumber; Customer-type (polymorphic) lookups are not supported. Creating a calculated column needs Write on the Field Security Profile table. Learn's training says the Calculated behavior "will eventually be discontinued" and recommends the Formula data type, but gives no date.
  • Rollup jobs (Settings > Advanced settings > System Jobs > Recurring System Jobs; administrators only): Mass Calculate Rollup Field is one per column and runs once, by default 12 hours after the column is created or updated. Calculate Rollup Field is one per table, incremental, with a default minimum recurrence of 1 hour. Administrators can postpone, pause, resume or modify them but cannot cancel or delete them.
  • Recalculate: select the calculator icon on the form, then Recalculate. It needs Write on the table and the row (not on the child table), works online only, and is capped at 50,000 related rows and hierarchy depth 10.
  • Rollup behavior: each rollup adds <name>_date and <name>_state columns. It is aggregated as the system user, so everyone sees the same value (hide it with column security). The documented maximum number of rollups differs between pages (200 per environment and 50 per table, adjustable with MaxRollupFieldsPerOrg and MaxRollupFieldsPerEntity, against 100 and 10), so do not memorise a number.
  • Formula columns: the formula decides the output type, and you may edit it later only if the type stays the same. Numbers default to Decimal (precision 0 to 10, default 2); Float(), Sqrt, Ln, Power, Exp or ^ produce a float. Null numbers count as 0 (calculated columns return null). Now() is user local; UTCNow() is time-zone independent. Avoid mixing calculated and formula columns.
  • Functions: only a subset of Power Fx works, for example Abs, Concatenate, DateAdd, DateDiff, If, IfError, Left, Len, Lower, Max, Min, Mid, Round, Switch, Text, Trim, Upper, Value. Not supported: Today, Date, DateValue, Time, Filter, LookUp, IsMatch, Coalesce, Proper, Concat, Patch, Collect.
  • Text rules: Text() and Value() work with whole numbers only. A number cannot be passed to a string function or joined implicitly with text, and Text() on a number needs a format argument.
  • Get formula suggestions turns a plain-language request into a suggested formula. Preview It works only in US regions, for a single table, and only when the admin setting AI suggestions for formula columns (Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > the environment > Settings > Product > Features) is on. The default is off.
Text(Quantity, "#") & " units"            // valid
Quantity & " units"                        // invalid: no implicit number-to-text
Text(Quantity) & " units"                  // invalid: one-argument Text on a number
Concatenate(Quantity, " units")            // invalid: a number in a string function
DateAdd(UTCNow(), -1, TimeUnit.Years)      // valid DateTime formula

Choosing: an always-current derived value on the same row or its parent is a formula column (preferred for new work) or a calculated column (pick calculated when the result must be Currency). Aggregating child rows over 1:N is a rollup; only a rollup aggregates. None of the three triggers a workflow.

Exam traps
  • Calculated and formula columns are computed when the row is read; a rollup is scheduled and stored, so it can lag by 12 hours (first calculation) or an hour (incremental).
  • Calculated chains stop at 5; formula depth stops at 10 (a chain of formula columns that refer to other formula or rollup columns); a formula is capped at 1,000 characters.
  • A formula column cannot output Currency, and Text(number) with one argument fails.
  • A rollup cannot cross an N:N relationship or aggregate another rollup.
  • Calculated function names are uppercase (DIFFINDAYS, CONCAT); formula columns use Power Fx names (DateDiff, Concatenate).

Evaluate use cases for business logic

Learn frames the choice as business rules (simple, no-code validations on forms), Power Fx formula columns (real-time computed values), Dataverse functions (reusable server-side logic with parameters, preview) and Power Automate (asynchronous workflows across apps and services). Use declarative options before code.

RequirementUseWhy the alternatives fail
Block a save in every app and flow (a High priority request needs a technician)Business rule, Table scope, Show Error MessageA cloud flow runs after the save; All Forms scope is client only; a column cannot block a save
Days open, line total or any derived value that is always currentFormula column (or calculated)A rollup is scheduled; a flow is asynchronous; a rule's simple formula handles only two columns
Result must be CurrencyCalculated columnFormula columns cannot output Currency
Sum, count, min, max or average of child rowsRollup columnCalculated and formula columns do not aggregate child rows
Guided stages with required fieldsBusiness process flowA flow has no stage UI; a rule cannot gate stages
Email, approval, connectors, schedule, work after the saveCloud flow (§3.1)Rules and columns cannot call connectors or wait
Reusable Power Fx with parameters for apps and flowsDataverse function (Preview)A formula column has no parameters
Hide a form tab or section; use related rows in the formJavaScript (client API)Business rules cannot change tabs or sections or read related rows
Complex, transactional or high-volume server logicPlug-in (C#)Rules are too simple; flows are asynchronous
Replace an old background workflowCloud flowClassic workflows are legacy
  • Sync or async: a cloud flow cannot run synchronously and cannot veto a save. Table-scope business rules, synchronous plug-ins and classic real-time workflows run inside the save.
  • Dataverse functions (formerly instant low-code plug-ins) are created with Solutions > New > Automation > Function and called on demand from canvas apps, custom pages and flows.
  • Business skills give agents natural-language guidance. They are not executable code and never enforce a rule.
ItemStatus
Business rules, business process flows, calculated, rollup and formula columnsGA
Get formula suggestionsPreview US regions only; admin setting off by default
Dataverse functionsPreview
Automated low-code plug-insStill documented as pre-release (preview)
Instant low-code plug-insDeprioritized and not delivered as a feature; replaced by functions
Classic workflows (background and real-time)Legacy: Learn says to create flows instead; no retirement date is documented
Business skillsPreview
Exam traps
  • "Power Fx" does not mean generally available everywhere: formula columns are GA, while Dataverse functions and low-code plug-ins are preview.
  • A cloud flow never blocks a save. Pick a Table-scope business rule or a plug-in when the save must be rejected.
  • A BPF guides people through stages; it does not run logic by itself.
  • Do not choose a plug-in or JavaScript when a business rule, column or flow already meets the requirement.

sections.title: Study habits that work
sections.html:
• Build, then read. Do the task in the product first, then read the section to see what you missed.
  • Memorize exact names: menu paths, settings, limits, roles and (for code) object, method and attribute names.
  • Practise the decision, not just the definition. For every feature write "choose it when / do not choose it when".
  • Keep a trap log. Every missed question becomes one line: what I picked and why it was wrong.
  • Use the Missed filter in Quick drill until it is empty, then re-take the full exam.
  • Read documentation dated 2026. Features were renamed and moved between preview and GA recently.

sections.title: Exam-day plan
sections.html:
The week before

  • Take the full timed practice exam twice, a few days apart; fix every skill rated below 4.
  • Skim the cheat sheets and your trap log — do not start new topics.
  • Run the exam sandbox (aka.ms/examdemo) once so flagging, the review screen and the case-study layout are familiar.
  • Online exam? Run Pearson VUE's system test, clear your desk and room and have government ID ready. Test center? Confirm the address and arrival time.
  • Re-check the official study guide in case Microsoft revised the skills list.

During the exam

TopicApproach
PacingWith 40–60 questions in 120 minutes you have roughly 2.0–3.0 minutes per question. Do not spend more than about 3 minutes on one item in the first pass.
First passAnswer what you know, flag what you do not. Answer every question before time runs out — an unanswered item cannot earn credit.
EliminationCross out answers that use retired, renamed or wrong-direction features. Many questions have two plausible options — look for the deciding constraint (GA versus Preview, required role, prerequisite, order of steps).
Multi-selectCount how many answers are requested ("Select TWO"); each must be independently correct.
Configuration itemsCheck the exact setting, scope, role or sequence the requirement names before choosing between similar options.
Case studiesSkim the questions first, then read the scenario for the requirements and constraints that matter. Re-read the exhibit instead of relying on memory. Breaks are allowed in case studies, but you cannot return to questions seen before the break.
Microsoft Learn buttonOn associate and expert exams Microsoft Learn opens in a split screen (no extra time; Q&A, practice assessments and your profile are blocked). Use it only to confirm one detail with Ctrl+F; if you cannot find it in about 90 seconds, make your best choice and flag it.
BreaksThe clock keeps running during a break, and after a break you cannot go back to earlier questions. You cannot break in the middle of a lab or a problem/solution question set. Use the restroom before you start.
ReviewUse the review screen for flagged items. Change an answer only if you can name the specific fact that makes your first choice wrong.
